content.content:
1	# Authoring `@pantoken/components`
2	
3	`@pantoken/components` is the semantic RSCSS CSS API — a parameterized generator, not hand-written
4	CSS. Each documented record is one file; the bucket `index.ts` is a barrel + registry, not a monolith.
5	
6	## Source layout
7	
8	- `src/components/<name>.ts` + `index.ts` (`COMPONENTS` registry).
9	- `src/utilities/<name>.ts` + `index.ts` (`UTILITIES`).
10	- `src/rules/{base,prose}.ts` + `index.ts` (`RULES`).
11	- `src/declarations/<name>.ts` + `index.ts` (`DECLARATIONS`).
12	- `src/lib/`: `helpers.ts` (ns/scope/glyph consts/spacing scales/`ComponentOptions`/`DEFAULT_PREFIX`),
13	  `define.ts` (`defineComponent`/`defineUtility`/`defineRule`/`defineDeclaration`), `aliases.ts`
14	  (`withSizeAliases`/`withAliases`), `css.ts` (the identity `css` tag), `headings.ts`,
15	  `field-controls.ts`.
16	
17	## Authoring a record
18	
19	```ts
20	export const foo = defineComponent({
21	  name,
22	  summary,
23	  modifiers,
24	  parts,
25	  cssProperties,
26	  examples,
27	  structure,
28	  demo,
29	  css: (p) =>
30	    // prettier-ignore
31	    css`…css body…`,
32	});
33	export const fooCss = foo.css;
34	```
35	
36	- The doc comment is **metadata** — plain strings, no backtick/`${` escaping.
37	- Only the `css` body stays a template literal. **Tag it with `css` and put a `// prettier-ignore`
38	  line right before it** (before the template for a direct arrow body, before `return` for a block).
39	  oxfmt treats `css` and `styled` tagged templates as embedded CSS and corrupts interpolated
40	  selectors (`${p}foo.-mod` → `${p}foo .-mod`, a different meaning) otherwise. Setting
41	  `embeddedLanguageFormatting` to off does **not** stop it. See the engineering log.
42	- Add the record to its bucket `index.ts`. For `COMPONENTS` the order is **load-bearing** — it matches
43	  the `componentsCss()` concat order, not alphabetical.
44	
45	## The modifier convention (key-value RSCSS compound)
46	
47	- Modifiers are `.${p}<comp>.-<prop>-<val>`, aligned to InstUI prop names
48	  (`-color-secondary`, `-size-sm`, `-shape-circle`, `-variant-title-page`).
49	- Booleans are the prop name alone, presence = true (`-clickable`, `-condensed`). A default-on boolean
50	  toggled off **inverts**: `-without-background`, `-without-border`.
51	- Sizes use one scale `-size-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}`, emitted with both short and long spellings as
52	  first-class aliases via `withSizeAliases()`.
53	- Nested elements are **unprefixed short classes scoped as descendants** (`.instui-menu .item`), not
54	  BEM `__`. Non-nested structural parts that can't be descendant-scoped are **flat prefixed**
55	  (`.instui-badge-wrapper`). A guard test rejects `__` and `--`.
56	- Avoid hyphen-then-digit tokens (`-2xs` needs escaping); keep tokens letter-leading.
57	
58	## Deprecated aliases (auto-discovered, always functional)
59	
60	- Author a modifier's metadata with `deprecated: "{@link -canonical}"`. `withAliases` reads that and
61	  clones each canonical rule under the alias name. There is no hardcoded pairs list.
62	- **A deprecated modifier must be a functional alias — never a doc-only noop** (user's absolute rule).

# Authoring `@pantoken/components`

`@pantoken/components` is the semantic RSCSS CSS API — a parameterized generator, not hand-written
CSS. Each documented record is one file; the bucket `index.ts` is a barrel + registry, not a monolith.

## Source layout

- `src/components/<name>.ts` + `index.ts` (`COMPONENTS` registry).
- `src/utilities/<name>.ts` + `index.ts` (`UTILITIES`).
- `src/rules/{base,prose}.ts` + `index.ts` (`RULES`).
- `src/declarations/<name>.ts` + `index.ts` (`DECLARATIONS`).
- `src/lib/`: `helpers.ts` (ns/scope/glyph consts/spacing scales/`ComponentOptions`/`DEFAULT_PREFIX`),
  `define.ts` (`defineComponent`/`defineUtility`/`defineRule`/`defineDeclaration`), `aliases.ts`
  (`withSizeAliases`/`withAliases`), `css.ts` (the identity `css` tag), `headings.ts`,
  `field-controls.ts`.

## Authoring a record

```ts
export const foo = defineComponent({
  name,
  summary,
  modifiers,
  parts,
  cssProperties,
  examples,
  structure,
  demo,
  css: (p) =>
    // prettier-ignore
    css`…css body…`,
});
export const fooCss = foo.css;
```

- The doc comment is **metadata** — plain strings, no backtick/`${` escaping.
- Only the `css` body stays a template literal. **Tag it with `css` and put a `// prettier-ignore`
  line right before it** (before the template for a direct arrow body, before `return` for a block).
  oxfmt treats `css` and `styled` tagged templates as embedded CSS and corrupts interpolated
  selectors (`${p}foo.-mod` → `${p}foo .-mod`, a different meaning) otherwise. Setting
  `embeddedLanguageFormatting` to off does **not** stop it. See the engineering log.
- Add the record to its bucket `index.ts`. For `COMPONENTS` the order is **load-bearing** — it matches
  the `componentsCss()` concat order, not alphabetical.

## The modifier convention (key-value RSCSS compound)

- Modifiers are `.${p}<comp>.-<prop>-<val>`, aligned to InstUI prop names
  (`-color-secondary`, `-size-sm`, `-shape-circle`, `-variant-title-page`).
- Booleans are the prop name alone, presence = true (`-clickable`, `-condensed`). A default-on boolean
  toggled off **inverts**: `-without-background`, `-without-border`.
- Sizes use one scale `-size-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}`, emitted with both short and long spellings as
  first-class aliases via `withSizeAliases()`.
- Nested elements are **unprefixed short classes scoped as descendants** (`.instui-menu .item`), not
  BEM `__`. Non-nested structural parts that can't be descendant-scoped are **flat prefixed**
  (`.instui-badge-wrapper`). A guard test rejects `__` and `--`.
- Avoid hyphen-then-digit tokens (`-2xs` needs escaping); keep tokens letter-leading.

## Deprecated aliases (auto-discovered, always functional)

- Author a modifier's metadata with `deprecated: "{@link -canonical}"`. `withAliases` reads that and
  clones each canonical rule under the alias name. There is no hardcoded pairs list.
- **A deprecated modifier must be a functional alias — never a doc-only noop** (user's absolute rule).
- The alias post-processors run on the CSS **body only**, before the doc block is prepended, because
  the doc block's `{@link}` braces confuse the brace-based scanners. They anchor on the base class
  (`.instui-radio.-variant-toggle`), not the bare token, so a bare `.-canonical` match doesn't wrongly
  clone `:not(.-canonical)` or compound rules.

## `@scope` and child-combinator scoping

`scope(root, body, children?)` (in `helpers.ts`) rewrites element rules and wraps them in
`@scope (root) { … }`. Two constraints that bite:

1. Keep the component **root rule and every root-modifier-only rule (especially `-size-*`) outside**
   the scope, prefixed — because `withSizeAliases`/`withAliases` append twin rules at top level by
   scanning flat CSS; a `:scope.-size-*` twin emitted inside a scope block would be orphaned.
2. Never pass a body whose root token prefixes a sibling class (e.g. `.instui-progress` prefixes
   `.instui-progress-value`) — the string split would corrupt it to `:scope-value`. Keep flat
   siblings out of the scoped body.

`@scope`/`:is`/`:has`/`:where` are **not** namespacing tools — only a unique or prefixed name prevents
a collision. Scoping narrows intent and deep-nesting collisions; it isn't collision-proof.

## Icons

Glyphs render via a single generic `[class*="${p}icon-"]::before` mask painter (currentColor, 1em
box). A glyph class rides a host directly because `--pantoken-glyph` is a plain (non-`@property`)
custom prop that inherits into `::before`. So `<button class="instui-button -shape-square
-icon-arrow-right">` needs no nested icon span. Built-in component glyphs source from the shared
`--instui-icon-<name>` tokens via an `iconMask(name)` helper.

## Per-component checklist

Extend the record, update the drift-checked test, update the guide (`docs/guide/components.md`), and
add or update a demo. Then run `vp check --fix`, the component + demo tests, `check:publish`, and
`lint:markdown`. Browser-verify anything visual. Skip upstream tokens that are `@property`-registered
but value-less (being removed upstream) — don't invent them.

1	# Build, release, and the docs site
2	
3	## Use the `vp` toolchain, never pnpm directly
4	
5	- `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` are **global** bins. Run tasks via `vp run <task>`, execute bins via `vp exec
6	[-F <glob>] <bin>`.
7	- **Package scripts must never shell out to `pnpm`.** CI (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) provides `vp`
8	  via `voidzero-dev/setup-vp` but **not** `pnpm` on PATH, so a `pnpm run …` inside any script breaks
9	  the docs deploy with `pnpm: command not found`. Local dev has pnpm, so a top-level `pnpm run X` is
10	  fine — but scripts it calls must stay pnpm-free internally.
11	- `.css` formatting: `vp fmt` (oxc) is JS/TS/JSON only and no-ops on `.css`. Stylelint owns `.css` —
12	  `lint:css` runs `stylelint --fix`, wired into `ready` and the `vite.config.ts` `staged` hook.
13	
14	## The gate
15	
16	- `pnpm run ready` — the pass/fail gate. It's a `vp` task DAG (`ready:all`), not a serial chain:
17	  `build:all` runs once, then `check:all` (`vp check`), `test:all` (`vp run -r test`), `lint:css`,
18	  `lint:js`, `validate:generated:only`, and `lint:markdown` fan out concurrently. Everything that reads
19	  generated output depends on `build:all`, so generation happens exactly once (no concurrent codegen
20	  race). Must pass before you're done.
21	- `pnpm run check:publish` — the publish gate (`gate:publish`): `gate:repository` (asserts every
22	  publishable manifest has the `repository.url` npm OIDC provenance needs), `gate:publint`, and
23	  `gate:attw`. Publint/attw depend on `build:all`; the repository check is a pure manifest read.
24	- **CI runs the same checks on every PR** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): `build` → parallel
25	  `typecheck`/`test`/`lint`/`publint`/`attw`, plus a `repository` job and a `commitlint` job that lints
26	  the PR's commit range. Jobs share a persisted vp task cache (`node_modules/.vite/task-cache`), so the
27	  `build` job warms it and downstream jobs restore it and re-materialize generated dirs from cache.
28	- **`publint`/`attw` are scoped to what the PR touches.** `scripts/release/changed-packages.ts` maps
29	  the diff against the base branch to the affected publishable packages (each changed package plus its
30	  workspace dependents, since a dependency change can break a dependent's pack/types), and the jobs run
31	  `vp exec -F <those>` instead of packing all ~70. A change to a global file (root `package.json`,
32	  lockfile, `vite.config.ts`, …) widens back to the full gate; a change touching no publishable package
33	  skips them.
34	- **Commit messages are conventional-commit-linted** locally by the `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` hook
35	  (`vp exec commitlint --edit`) and in CI by the `commitlint` job.
36	- Release automation uses Changesets and package-tag workflows in
37	  `.github/workflows/release.yml`. That workflow verifies a clean build/typecheck/test + `gate:repository`,
38	  then scopes the pack-heavy `publint`/`attw` gates to exactly the publish set (the full `ready` already
39	  ran on the merge-to-main the tag points at).
40	- Use `pnpm run release:version` to apply package changelog/version updates, then
41	  `vp run release:changelog:root` to rebuild the strict chronological root `CHANGELOG.md` before
42	  creating package tags.
43	- Generated artifacts are gitignored and reproduced on build: `platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
44	  `platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, and web-components `src/generated/`.
45	  `build:all` produces them before any gate that reads them runs.
46	
47	See `docs/internal/release-strategy.md` for the runbook, dist-tag mapping, prerelease flow, and npm
48	organization governance model.
49	
50	## Linting CSS
51	
52	Root `stylelint.config.js` runs error-only core rules plus `@cssdoc/stylelint-plugin`'s
53	`cssdoc/valid-doc-comments`; anchor-positioning props are ignored and `@scope` is allowed. A parallel
54	`eslint.config.js` runs `@cssdoc/eslint-plugin` (via `@eslint/css`) over the same `.css` (`lint:js`).
55	`lint:css` targets the web-components `src/**/*.css` sources and the generated components CSS.
56	
57	## The docs site
58	
59	`docs/` is a VitePress site (`@pantoken/docs`) with two locales — `root` (English, `/…`) and `hu`
60	(Magyar, `/hu/…`) — a symmetric prefix swap that VitePress's default routing already handles (don't
61	set a custom `i18nRouting`).
62	
63	- **Translation layer is `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`.** `LOCALES[locale]` holds every localizable UI
64	  string (nav/sidebar labels, `editText`, the theme selector, VitePress chrome labels, and local
65	  search). `config.ts` expands these into per-locale `themeConfig` (search is the exception — it lives
66	  in the global `themeConfig.search.options.locales`). Add new UI strings here, never inline.
67	- **Block-level API translation.** `build-api-locales.ts` doesn't translate whole `.md` files — it
68	  runs `segment-markdown.ts` to split each generated page into blocks: `prose` (descriptions,
69	  remarks, `@example` captions, cssdoc table Description cells), `glossary` (section headings,
70	  stability-badge pills, table column labels), and `preserve` (code fences, signatures, breadcrumbs,
71	  token tables). Only prose carries a content key, so a page's prose survives the scaffolding churn
72	  (badge flips, token-value changes, signature edits) that used to bust a whole-file key. `glossary`
73	  blocks always go through the deterministic `GlossaryTranslationAdapter` (keyless, never cached);
74	  `preserve` blocks are emitted verbatim.
75	- **The committed cache carries the prose; CI serves it.** The translation memory
76	  (`docs/i18n-cache/hu.api.json`) is content-addressed and adapter-agnostic, so a claude-authored
77	  prose entry is served to a `glossary` build as a plain cache hit. The workflow: run
78	  `pnpm run docs:api:locales:claude` **locally** to author prose (a cold run is bounded to ~30–40
79	  batched `claude -p` calls, resumable via the memory's autosave), then commit `hu.api.json`. CI's
80	  `docs:build` runs the `glossary` adapter, which serves that prose from cache and only ever fills
81	  structural headings/labels. Brand-new prose that isn't cached yet passes through as English — the
82	  glossary **never** caches its own prose passthrough (that would permanently mask the block from a
83	  later claude run), so it stays a miss until claude authors it. Never wire `:claude` into CI.
84	- **Running the cold pass.** Each `claude -p` call cold-starts a full agent, and the dominant cost is
85	  the per-call bootstrap — loading MCP servers, plugins, and project settings — not the translation
86	  itself (it dwarfs even a small model's inference). So the `:claude` tasks pass
87	  `--model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources user`: a fast model, **no
88	  MCP**, and user settings only (keeps auth, drops project/local hooks). That cuts each call from
89	  minutes to a few seconds. Override by editing the task or exporting your own
90	  `DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND_ARGS` before a direct `node scripts/…` run (`DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND`
91	  overrides the `claude` binary itself). Either task logs progress (`… N/M labels + prose blocks
92	translated`) and saves the memory after **each** chunk, so it's resumable — a kill or crash keeps
93	  completed chunks and a re-run serves them from cache.
94	- **The cold pass is generation-bound, so it runs chunks concurrently.** Once MCP is stripped, the
95	  wall-clock cost is the model streaming translations, not startup — so `ClaudeCodeTranslationAdapter`
96	  runs up to `DOCS_TRANSLATION_CONCURRENCY` (default 5) `claude -p` calls at once. Prose is batched at
97	  `DOCS_TRANSLATION_BATCH_BUDGET` chars/request (default 4k) — small enough that each JSON response
98	  stays reliable and progress is fine-grained, with the pool hiding the per-call startup. A chunk that
99	  errors is logged and skipped (its blocks stay uncached and retry next run), never sinking the whole
100	  run. Raise concurrency for more speed if you're not rate-limited; lower the budget if a run trips the
101	  per-item fallback (the model dropping a key from a large response).
102	
103	## The cssdoc integration
104	
105	pantoken consumes `@cssdoc/*` from **npm** (catalog entries; consumers use `catalog:`), not a local
106	workspace link. `docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts` is a thin wrapper: it builds pantoken's `resolveToken`
107	(syntax + value + local vars) and `resolveDemo` hooks, then calls `@cssdoc/typedoc`'s `emitCssApi`,
108	and keeps the `unknownReferences` drift guard. All page/index/sidebar rendering lives in
109	`@cssdoc/markdown`. The live `<div class="css-example">` preview is pantoken's own
110	`@pantoken/typedoc-plugin-live-example`, kept out of `@cssdoc/markdown` so the upstream stays generic.
111	
112	**Catalog gotcha:** cssdoc packages reference `catalog:` deps; if cssdoc adds a new one, pantoken's
113	catalog must carry it too, or install fails with `ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND_FOR_SPEC`.
114	
115	## The nested-`vp`-spawn limitation
116	
117	Under `vpr docs:dev`, VitePress runs _under_ `vp`. Any `vp run …` / `vp pack` spawned from **inside**
118	that process dies with `Failed to spawn process: Invalid argument (os error 22)` on a cache miss. A
119	direct `node scripts/x.ts` is unaffected. So:
120	
121	- The docs orchestrator's `upstream[].build` uses `["node","scripts/generate.ts"]` (cwd = the package
122	  dir), not a nested `vp run`.
123	- The CSS-API node runs `["node","scripts/build-css-api.ts"]` (cwd `docs`).
124	- `@pantoken/web-components`' `register()` bundle genuinely needs `vp pack` (which also can't nest), so
125	  it's not in the live orchestrator — rebuild it in a separate top-level shell
126	  (`vpr @pantoken/web-components#build`); `outputWatchPaths` on its `dist` bridges the change into HMR.
127	
128	A `vp run X && vp run Y` chain _inside_ a package.json script is fine — that's a top-level
129	script-runner context, not a spawn from within the running VitePress process.

(syntax + value + local vars) and `resolveDemo` hooks, then calls `@cssdoc/typedoc`'s `emitCssApi`,
and keeps the `unknownReferences` drift guard. All page/index/sidebar rendering lives in
`@cssdoc/markdown`. The live `<div class="css-example">` preview is pantoken's own
`@pantoken/typedoc-plugin-live-example`, kept out of `@cssdoc/markdown` so the upstream stays generic.

**Catalog gotcha:** cssdoc packages reference `catalog:` deps; if cssdoc adds a new one, pantoken's
catalog must carry it too, or install fails with `ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND_FOR_SPEC`.

## The nested-`vp`-spawn limitation

Under `vpr docs:dev`, VitePress runs _under_ `vp`. Any `vp run …` / `vp pack` spawned from **inside**
that process dies with `Failed to spawn process: Invalid argument (os error 22)` on a cache miss. A
direct `node scripts/x.ts` is unaffected. So:

- The docs orchestrator's `upstream[].build` uses `["node","scripts/generate.ts"]` (cwd = the package
  dir), not a nested `vp run`.
- The CSS-API node runs `["node","scripts/build-css-api.ts"]` (cwd `docs`).
- `@pantoken/web-components`' `register()` bundle genuinely needs `vp pack` (which also can't nest), so
  it's not in the live orchestrator — rebuild it in a separate top-level shell
  (`vpr @pantoken/web-components#build`); `outputWatchPaths` on its `dist` bridges the change into HMR.

A `vp run X && vp run Y` chain _inside_ a package.json script is fine — that's a top-level
script-runner context, not a spawn from within the running VitePress process.

1	/**
2	 * The `--instui-elevation-*` shadow scale. Helpers only — NOT a documented record and not in any
3	 * registry: `componentsCss()` leads its sheet with `elevationCss()` so the shadows components
4	 * reference (modal, alert, menu) resolve from `components.css` alone.
5	 *
6	 * @module
7	 */
8	
9	/** Per-level geometry (`offset-x offset-y blur`) for the [tighter, wider] shadow layers. */
10	const ELEVATION_GEOMETRY: Record<string, [tight: string, wide: string]> = {
11	  resting: ["0 0.0625rem 0.125rem", "0 0.0625rem 0.1875rem"],
12	  above: ["0 0.1875rem 0.375rem", "0 0.1875rem 0.375rem"],
13	  topmost: ["0 0.375rem 0.4375rem", "0 0.625rem 1.75rem"],
14	};
15	
16	/** Aliases InstUI ships alongside the primary level names. */
17	const ELEVATION_ALIASES: Record<string, keyof typeof ELEVATION_GEOMETRY> = {
18	  depth1: "resting",
19	  depth2: "above",
20	  depth3: "topmost",
21	  card: "resting",
22	  cardHover: "topmost",
23	};
24	
25	/**
26	 * Every elevation level and alias emitted as `--instui-elevation-<name>` (`resting`, `above`,
27	 * `topmost`, `depth1`–`depth3`, `card`, `cardHover`). Derived from the geometry + alias maps.
28	 */
29	export const ELEVATION_NAMES: readonly string[] = [
30	  ...Object.keys(ELEVATION_GEOMETRY),
31	  ...Object.keys(ELEVATION_ALIASES),
32	];
33	
34	// The tighter layer takes the softer colour, the wider layer the stronger one — InstUI's "lifted" look.
35	const ELEVATION_COLOR_STRONG = "var(--instui-color-drop-shadow-shadow-color1)";
36	const ELEVATION_COLOR_SOFT = "var(--instui-color-drop-shadow-shadow-color2)";
37	const elevationShadow = ([tight, wide]: [string, string]): string =>
38	  `${tight} ${ELEVATION_COLOR_SOFT}, ${wide} ${ELEVATION_COLOR_STRONG}`;
39	
40	/**
41	 * The `--instui-elevation-*` name/value pairs (each a multi-layer `box-shadow`). Values reference the
42	 * themed drop-shadow colour tokens, so they adapt per theme wherever a token sheet is loaded.
43	 *
44	 * @returns One `[customProperty, value]` pair per level and alias.
45	 */
46	export function elevationDeclarations(): [name: string, value: string][] {
47	  const levels: [string, [string, string]][] = [
48	    ...Object.entries(ELEVATION_GEOMETRY),
49	    ...Object.entries(ELEVATION_ALIASES).map(([alias, base]): [string, [string, string]] => [
50	      alias,
51	      ELEVATION_GEOMETRY[base],
52	    ]),
53	  ];
54	  return levels.map(([name, geo]) => [`--instui-elevation-${name}`, elevationShadow(geo)]);
55	}
56	
57	/**
58	 * Build the elevation token block: `<selector> { --instui-elevation-*: … }`. Shipped inside
59	 * `components.css` (so shadows are intrinsic — no plugin, no extra import), and reusable by other
60	 * layered outputs (e.g. the Pendo renderer) via the `selector` option.
61	 *
62	 * @param options - `selector` — the rule selector (default `:root`).
63	 * @returns The CSS string.
64	 *
65	 * @example
66	 * ```ts
67	 * import { elevationCss } from "@pantoken/components";
68	 *
69	 * elevationCss(); // ":root { --instui-elevation-resting: …; --instui-elevation-above: …; … }"
70	 * ```
71	 *
72	 * @demo self:elevation
73	 */
74	export function elevationCss(options: { selector?: string } = {}): string {
75	  const selector = options.selector ?? ":root";
76	  const body = elevationDeclarations()
77	    .map(([name, value]) => `  ${name}: ${value};`)
78	    .join("\n");
79	  return `${selector} {\n${body}\n}\n`;
80	}

3	 * out of the box when pantoken owns the page. The resting element carries a transparent ring + a

5	 * zero-specificity `:where()`, so any component style overrides without `!important`.

9	 * (the bespoke builder `base.css` calls directly) and a {@link Definition}-shaped {@link focus} object
10	 * so the registry + `validate()` can treat it uniformly.

14	import { css } from "../lib/css.ts";
15	import type { Definition } from "../lib/define.ts";

21	 * @class :focus-visible
22	 * @summary The focus-outline system: the \`--instui-focus-outline-*\` custom properties (declared on \`:root\`) plus the \`:focus-visible\` ring every focusable gets, and opt-in tuning classes.
23	 * @modifier -focus-color-success — Success-coloured ring.

27	 * @modifier -focus-within — Ring the element while a descendant is focused.
28	 * @modifier -without-focus-animation — Disable the ring's grow-in animation.
29	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color — The ring colour once focus is visible (the themed info colour).
30	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-start — The resting, transparent ring colour the outline transitions from.
31	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-width — The outline width of the ring.
32	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-offset — The gap between the element's edge and the ring when focused.
33	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-radius — The ring's corner radius when focused.
34	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-style — The outline line style (solid).
35	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-transition — The transition that animates the ring's colour and offset in.
36	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-success — The ring colour for the \`-focus-color-success\` modifier.
37	 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-danger — The ring colour for the \`-focus-color-danger\` modifier.

54	 * the themed shared focus tokens; the transition, line style, and inset are constants.
55	 *

57	 */
58	export function focusOutlineDeclarations(): [name: string, value: string][] {
59	  return [
60	    ["--instui-focus-outline-color", focusShared("info-color")],
61	    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-start", "transparent"],
62	    ["--instui-focus-outline-width", focusShared("width")],
63	    ["--instui-focus-outline-offset", focusShared("offset")],
64	    ["--instui-focus-outline-radius", "var(--instui-border-radius-md)"],

68	    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-danger", focusShared("danger-color")],

87	    `  transition: var(--instui-focus-outline-transition);`,
88	    `}`,

90	    `  outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color);`,
91	    `  outline-offset: var(--instui-focus-outline-offset);`,
92	    `  border-radius: var(--instui-focus-outline-radius);`,
93	    `}`,

95	    `:where(.-focus-color-danger):where(:focus-visible) { outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color-danger); }`,
96	    `:where(.-focus-color-inverse):where(:focus-visible) { outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color-inverse); }`,
97	    `:where(.-focus-position-inset):where(:focus-visible) { outline-offset: var(--instui-focus-outline-inset); }`,
98	    `:where(.-focus-within):where(:focus-within) {`,
99	    `  outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color);`,
100	    `  outline-offset: var(--instui-focus-outline-offset);`,
101	    `  border-radius: var(--instui-focus-outline-radius);`,
102	    `}`,
103	    `:where(.-without-focus-animation) { transition: none; }`,
104	  ].join("\n");
105	}

108	 * Build the focus-outline block: the `--instui-focus-outline-*` token defs plus the ring rules.
109	 * Baked into `base.css` (so focusables get the ring out of the box), and reusable by other layered
110	 * outputs (e.g. the Pendo renderer) via the `selector`/`tokenSelector` options.
111	 *

113	 *   (default `:where(:root)`).
114	 * @returns The CSS string.
115	 *
116	 * @demo self:focus-outline
117	 */

120	): string {
121	  const tokenSelector = options.tokenSelector ?? ":where(:root)";
122	  const decls = focusOutlineDeclarations()
123	    .map(([name, value]) => `  ${name}: ${value};`)
124	    .join("\n");
125	  // prettier-ignore
126	  return css`${FOCUS_DOC}\n${tokenSelector} {\n${decls}\n}\n\n${focusOutlineRules(options.selector)}\n`;
127	}
128

130	 * The {@link Definition}-shaped view of the focus declaration, so it can sit in the DECLARATIONS
131	 * registry and be checked by `validate()`. `css()`/`rules()` delegate to {@link focusOutlineCss} (its
132	 * default `instui`-prefixed output is a single well-formed declaration record).
133	 */
134	export const focus: Definition = {
135	  name: "focus",
136	  kind: "declaration",
137	  rules: () => focusOutlineCss(),
138	  css: () => focusOutlineCss(),
139	};

/**
 * The focus-outline system — the InstUI focus ring, intrinsic to `base.css` so every focusable gets it
 * out of the box when pantoken owns the page. The resting element carries a transparent ring + a
 * transition, and `:focus-visible` reveals the colour and grows the offset. All rules are
 * zero-specificity `:where()`, so any component style overrides without `!important`.
 *
 * This is the one documented `@declaration` record, but it can't use `defineDeclaration` (its CSS is a
 * token block on one selector plus ring rules on another). Instead it exposes {@link focusOutlineCss}
 * (the bespoke builder `base.css` calls directly) and a {@link Definition}-shaped {@link focus} object
 * so the registry + `validate()` can treat it uniformly.
 *
 * @module
 */
import { css } from "../lib/css.ts";
import type { Definition } from "../lib/define.ts";

/** The focus declaration's cssdoc doc comment (authored inline; the CSS body follows in {@link focusOutlineCss}). */
// prettier-ignore
const FOCUS_DOC = css`/**
 * @declaration focus
 * @class :focus-visible
 * @summary The focus-outline system: the \`--instui-focus-outline-*\` custom properties (declared on \`:root\`) plus the \`:focus-visible\` ring every focusable gets, and opt-in tuning classes.
 * @modifier -focus-color-success — Success-coloured ring.
 * @modifier -focus-color-danger — Danger-coloured ring.
 * @modifier -focus-color-inverse — Inverse (on-dark) ring.
 * @modifier -focus-position-inset — Draw the ring inset, inside the element's edge.
 * @modifier -focus-within — Ring the element while a descendant is focused.
 * @modifier -without-focus-animation — Disable the ring's grow-in animation.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color — The ring colour once focus is visible (the themed info colour).
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-start — The resting, transparent ring colour the outline transitions from.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-width — The outline width of the ring.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-offset — The gap between the element's edge and the ring when focused.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-radius — The ring's corner radius when focused.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-style — The outline line style (solid).
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-transition — The transition that animates the ring's colour and offset in.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-success — The ring colour for the \`-focus-color-success\` modifier.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-danger — The ring colour for the \`-focus-color-danger\` modifier.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-color-inverse — The ring colour for the \`-focus-color-inverse\` (on-dark) modifier.
 * @cssproperty --instui-focus-outline-inset — The outline offset used when \`-focus-position-inset\` draws the ring inside the edge.
 * @a11y Every focusable element gets a \`:focus-visible\` outline ring so keyboard users can see what's focused.
 * @example
 * <button class="instui-button -focus-color-danger">Delete</button>
 * @demo self:focus-outline
 */`;

/** The elements the ring applies to by default (the common interactive/focusable elements). */
export const FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR = "a, button, input, select, textarea, summary, [tabindex]";

const focusShared = (name: string): string =>
  `var(--instui-component-shared-tokens-focus-outline-${name})`;

/**
 * The `--instui-focus-outline-*` name/value pairs the ring rules read. Colour/width/offset reference
 * the themed shared focus tokens; the transition, line style, and inset are constants.
 *
 * @returns One `[customProperty, value]` pair per focus-ring variable.
 */
export function focusOutlineDeclarations(): [name: string, value: string][] {
  return [
    ["--instui-focus-outline-color", focusShared("info-color")],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-start", "transparent"],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-width", focusShared("width")],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-offset", focusShared("offset")],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-radius", "var(--instui-border-radius-md)"],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-style", "solid"],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-transition", "outline-color 0.2s, outline-offset 0.25s"],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-success", focusShared("success-color")],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-danger", focusShared("danger-color")],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-color-inverse", focusShared("on-color")],
    ["--instui-focus-outline-inset", "0rem"],
  ];
}

/**
 * The focus-ring rules for a given focusable selector: a transparent resting ring that transitions in
 * on `:focus-visible`, plus the `-focus-color-*` / `-focus-position-inset` / `-focus-within` /

    `  outline-offset: 0;`,

    `  outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color);`,
    `  outline-offset: var(--instui-focus-outline-offset);`,
    `  border-radius: var(--instui-focus-outline-radius);`,

    `:where(.-focus-color-success):where(:focus-visible) { outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color-success); }`,
    `:where(.-focus-color-danger):where(:focus-visible) { outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color-danger); }`,
    `:where(.-focus-color-inverse):where(:focus-visible) { outline-color: var(--instui-focus-outline-color-inverse); }`,
    `:where(.-focus-position-inset):where(:focus-visible) { outline-offset: var(--instui-focus-outline-inset); }`,
    `:where(.-focus-within):where(:focus-within) {`,

    `  outline-offset: var(--instui-focus-outline-offset);`,

13	  /**
14	   * Also emit the deprecated InstUI-prop glyph aliases (`-render-icon-<name>`, `-render-custom-icon-<name>`)
15	   * as functional aliases of `-icon-<name>`. Off by default — turning it on roughly doubles the sheet, so
16	   * enable it only when you need markup written against the old `renderIcon`/`renderCustomIcon` prop names

22	/**
23	 * Build the icon-glyph stylesheet: one `.<prefix>-icon-<name>` class per icon that points
24	 * `--pantoken-glyph` at the matching `--instui-icon-<name>` token. Kept out of the component bundle
25	 * (it's large); ships as its own `icons.css`. Pass the icon names (e.g. from `@pantoken/icons`).
26	 *
27	 * @param names - Icon names without the `--instui-icon-` prefix (e.g. `["megaphone", "check"]`).
28	 * @param options - {@link IconGlyphsOptions} (adds `deprecatedAliases` to {@link ComponentOptions}).
29	 * @returns The CSS string.
30	 *
31	 * @example
32	 * ```ts
33	 * import { iconGlyphsCss } from "@pantoken/components";
34	 * import { icons } from "@pantoken/icons";
35	 *
36	 * const css = iconGlyphsCss(icons.map((i) => i.name)); // .-icon-megaphone { --pantoken-glyph: … }
37	 * ```
38	 *
39	 * This is the glyph-token half of the icon system (the `.-icon-<name>` modifiers, shipped as
40	 * `icons.css`); the `icon` utility is the painter half (the shared `::before`). They share the `icon`
41	 * demo.
42	 */
43	export function iconGlyphsCss(names: readonly string[], options: IconGlyphsOptions = {}): string {
44	  const prefix = options.prefix || "";
45	  const p = ns(prefix);
46	  void p; // glyph classes are prefix-independent modifiers (.-icon-<name>); consumed by any host.
47	  // The deprecated InstUI prop names that normalized to `-icon-<name>` (Pill's `renderIcon`, Alert's
48	  // `renderCustomIcon`). When `deprecatedAliases` is on, they're grouped onto the same rule as
49	  // FUNCTIONAL aliases (they set the same glyph var, and both contain the `-icon-` substring so the
50	  // shared painter + Alert's glyph pipe already fire) — otherwise omitted, which roughly halves the
51	  // sheet. They're `@deprecated` in each component's doc comment either way.
52	  const prefixes = options.deprecatedAliases
53	    ? ["-icon", "-render-icon", "-render-custom-icon"]
54	    : ["-icon"];
55	  const selectors = (name: string): string => prefixes.map((pre) => `.${pre}-${name}`).join(", ");
56	  const rules = names
57	    .map((name) => `${selectors(name)} { --pantoken-glyph: var(--instui-icon-${name}); }`)
58	    .join("\n");
59	  return `/* InstUI icon glyphs (@pantoken/components) — prefix: ${prefix} */\n${rules}\n`;
60	}

# The cssdoc comment system in pantoken

## 1. What a cssdoc block looks like — syntax, tags, structure

A cssdoc block is a CSS block comment (`/** … */`) that sits **immediately before the record's first CSS rule**. It opens with a **record tag** naming the record kind and name, then carries `@`-prefixed block tags. Each descriptive tag uses the form `@tag <name> — <description>` (an em-dash separates a modifier/part name from its prose).

**Two authoring styles coexist** (both produce identical output):

- **`.css`-authored** — real `.css` files under `src/components/` and `src/utilities/`, using the class-prefix sentinel `pfx-` (e.g. `.pfx-badge`). Example: `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/src/components/badge.css` lines 1-35 (the block), rules follow at line 36+.
- **`.ts`-inline-authored** — a `css`-tagged template literal in the `.ts` record, with `${p}` interpolating the prefix. Example: `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/src/components/button.ts` lines 10-42 (block inside `css\`` … at line 43 the `.${p}button {` rule starts). Note the mandatory `// prettier-ignore` on the line before the template (line 9).

The badge block (`badge.css:1-35`) is a good canonical example — it uses `@component`, `@summary`, many `@modifier`, `@pseudo`, `@cssproperty`, `@remarks`, `@animation`, `@example`, `@wrapper`, `@structure`, `@related`, `@demo`.

**Record kinds** (the opening tag, one per block): `@component`, `@utility`, `@rule`, `@declaration`. Examples of each:
- `@component` — `button.ts:11`, `badge.css:2`
- `@utility` — `formats/components/src/utilities/spacing.ts:28`
- `@rule` — `formats/components/src/rules/prose.ts:16`
- `@declaration` — `formats/components/src/declarations/focus.ts:20` (the only one; see §3)

**The `@structure` block** describes DOM shape with a mini-selector-tree syntax (`.pfx-badge-wrapper:opt { slot {} .pfx-badge {} }`), see `badge.css:27-32`.

### The canonical tag vocabulary

The single source of truth is **`@cssdoc/spec`** — `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/node_modules/.pnpm/@cssdoc+spec@0.7.8/node_modules/@cssdoc/spec/dist/index.mjs` (the `CSSDOC_TAGS` array). `@cssdoc/core` seeds its parser from it. Tags have a `kind` (`record` / `block` / `modifier` / `inline`), an optional `aliasFor`, and `allowMultiple`:

- **Record tags**: `component`, `utility`, `rule`, `declaration`, plus `name` (alt component opener).
- **Block tags** (single-use): `class`, `summary`, `remarks`, `privateRemarks`, `deprecated`, `since`, `group` (alias `category`), `defaultValue`, `structure`, `demo`, `usage`.
- **Block tags (repeatable, `allowMultiple`)**: `todo`, `example`, `see`, `modifier` (arg: modifier-name), `part`/`csspart` (part-name), `cssproperty`/`property` (custom-property), `cssstate`, `pseudo`, `wrapper` (part-name), `slot` (part-name), `tokens` (custom-property), `function`, `keyframes`/`animation`, `layer`, `container`, `supports`, `media`/`responsive`, `a11y`/`accessibility`, `compat`, `related`.
- **Modifier tags** (stability badges): `alpha`, `beta`, `experimental`, `internal`, `public`.
- **Inline tags**: `link` (`{@link -canonical}`), `inheritDoc`, `label`.

Aliases worth noting: `@accessibility`→`a11y`, `@csspart`→`part`, `@property`→`cssproperty`, `@animation`→`keyframes`, `@responsive`→`media`, `@category`→`group`.

The render/section order for docs pages is configured in `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/cssdoc.jsonc:5-31` (`accessibility, usage, demo, examples, structure, slots, modifiers, parts, shadowParts, pseudoElements, states, cssProperties, functions, animations, layers, conditions, tokensConsumed, compat, subcomponents, related, see`).

## 2. What makes a block "complete" vs "incomplete" — the validator

There is **no single "required-field schema"**; completeness is enforced by the linter `cssdoc/valid-doc-comments`, backed by **`@cssdoc/lint-core`** (`/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/node_modules/.pnpm/@cssdoc+lint-core@0.7.8/node_modules/@cssdoc/lint-core/dist/index.d.mts`). The `RuleName` union (line 6) is the definitive list of what can be "incomplete":

- **`missing-summary`** — a record **must** have `@summary`. This is the one universally-required tag.
- **`undocumented-modifier`** — a `.-modifier` selector exists in the CSS but has no `@modifier` tag.
- **`undocumented-part`** — a structural part/element selector exists but has no `@part`.
- **`name-not-in-css`** — a `@modifier`/`@part` documents a selector that doesn't appear in the CSS (stale doc).
- **`unknown-selector`** (a.k.a. `structure-unknown-selector`) — `@structure` references a class that isn't a real sibling/part.
- **`component-name-case` / `part-name-case`** — naming-case conventions.
- **`deprecated-requires-canonical`** — a `@deprecated` tag must `{@link}` a canonical (matches the "functional alias, never doc-only noop" rule in `docs/conventions/authoring.md:58-66`).
- **`invalid-default-value` / `invalid-property-value` / `invalid-fallback-value`** — `@cssproperty`/registered-property value checks.

So a block is **complete** when: it opens with the right record kind+name, has a `@summary`, and **every** modifier/part/pseudo/state present in the emitted CSS has a matching tag (no `undocumented-*`), with no stale references. All rules **default to `warn`**; pantoken raises them to error.

**Where it's wired in:**
- **stylelint** — `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/stylelint.config.js:17-21` (`plugins: ["@cssdoc/stylelint-plugin"]`, `"cssdoc/valid-doc-comments": true`). Runs on `renderers/web-components/src/**/*.css` and `formats/components/generated/*.css` plus the source overrides (lines 53-66).
- **eslint** — `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/eslint.config.js:10-24` (`@cssdoc/eslint-plugin` via `@eslint/css`, `"cssdoc/valid-doc-comments": "error"`) over `formats/components/src/{components,utilities}/*.css`, `formats/components/generated/*.css`, `renderers/web-components/src/**/*.css`.
- **test guard** — `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/tests/_validate.ts` uses the real `parseCssDocs` from `@cssdoc/core` to assert each `Definition` emits **exactly one** record of the declared kind/name (lines 24-33) plus token-reference drift.
- **Config** — options (`modifierConvention: "rscss"`, `inlineComments`, render/section order, `structureIgnore`) live in `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/cssdoc.jsonc`, auto-loaded per file. A scoped `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/cssdoc.jsonc` `extends` the root and adds a `providers` entry (`./src/generated/_records.css`) so single-file source linting can resolve **sibling** records referenced in `@structure`.
- The `@cssdoc/*` packages (`spec`, `core`, `config`, `lint-core`, `providers`, `embedded`, `markdown`, `typedoc`, `index`) are consumed from **npm via catalog**, not a workspace link (`docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md:104-113`).

## 3. Coverage — present vs absent across the tree

**`formats/components` is essentially fully documented already.** Every real record carries a block, in either its `.css` or its `.ts`. Mapping (relative to `formats/components/src/`):

**components/** — every component has a block. `.css`-authored (block in the `.css`): alert, avatar, badge, billboard, breadcrumb, byline, calendar, checkbox, close-button, context-view, file-drop, form-field(+group,+messages), img, in-place-edit, link, list, menu, metric, modal, pagination, pill, popover, progress(+circle), radio(+input-group), range-input, rating, side-nav-bar, spinner, table, tabs, tag, text, toggle-details, toggle-group, tooltip, tray, tree-browser, truncate. **`.ts`-inline-authored**: `button.ts`, `heading.ts`, `input-group.ts`, `number-input.ts`, `simple-select.ts`, `text-area.ts`, `text-input.ts`.

**utilities/** — documented: `icon.css`, `mask.css`, `screen-reader-content.css` (`.css` blocks); `layout.ts`, `responsive.ts`, `spacing.ts`, `view.ts` (`@utility` inline).

**rules/** — `base.ts` (`@rule base`) and `prose.ts` (`@rule prose`) both documented.

**declarations/** — `focus.ts` is the **only** documented declaration (`@declaration focus`, `focus.ts:19-44`). This is intentional per its own header (`focus.ts:5-7`).

**Intentionally NOT documented (helpers / bespoke — not gaps):**
- `declarations/elevation.ts` — explicitly "NOT a documented record and not in any registry" (`elevation.ts:1-7`); it's a shadow-scale helper.
- `components/select.ts` + `components/select.css` — the **only** component-shaped files with **no** cssdoc block, by design: "Bespoke (no cssdoc record, not in the COMPONENTS registry)" (`select.ts:2-4`), experimental `appearance: base-select`, gated behind `@supports`.

- All `index.ts` barrels.

**How the `.css` blocks reach the linter/docs:** `formats/components/scripts/component-styles.ts` compiles the `.css` files into `src/generated/component-styles.ts` string constants **retaining the `/** … */` doc comments** (they're load-bearing — `component-styles.ts:9-14`). The thin `.ts` wrappers (e.g. `badge.ts:5-8`) do `raw.replaceAll(SENTINEL, p)`. `define.ts` (`splitLeadingDocComment`, lines 48-52) splits the leading comment from the body so alias post-processors never see the `{@link}` braces.

**`plugins/pantoken/` — CSS-emitting but carrying ZERO cssdoc blocks (the real "absent" zone).** Every plugin emits CSS but none uses cssdoc records (`cssdoc_records=0` across the board):

These are token/primitive/utility CSS (e.g. `.instui-bg-primitive-color-*`, `.instui-stack-*`, `.instui-transition`), and none is currently wired into the stylelint/eslint cssdoc globs. If the sweep intends to document them, they'd be net-new blocks and would also need adding to the lint `files` globs to be validated.

## 4. Documentation conventions (the three docs)

- **`docs/conventions/authoring.md`** — how to author a `@pantoken/components` record: the `defineComponent`/`defineUtility`/`defineRule`/`defineDeclaration` shape (lines 19-34); "the doc comment is **metadata** — plain strings, no backtick/`${` escaping" (line 36); the `css`-tagged-template + `// prettier-ignore` rule (lines 37-41); the **rscss modifier convention** (`.-<prop>-<val>`, booleans, size scale, `withSizeAliases`) lines 43-56; **deprecated aliases** must be functional, authored as `deprecated: "{@link -canonical}"` (lines 58-66); `@scope`/scoping constraints; the per-component checklist (run `vp check --fix`, tests, `check:publish`, `lint:markdown`).

# The cssdoc comment system in pantoken

## 1. What a cssdoc block looks like — syntax, tags, structure

A cssdoc block is a CSS block comment (`/** … */`) that sits **immediately before the record's first CSS rule**. It opens with a **record tag** naming the record kind and name, then carries `@`-prefixed block tags. Each descriptive tag uses the form `@tag <name> — <description>` (an em-dash separates a modifier/part name from its prose).

**Two authoring styles coexist** (both produce identical output):

- **`.css`-authored** — real `.css` files under `src/components/` and `src/utilities/`, using the class-prefix sentinel `pfx-` (e.g. `.pfx-badge`). Example: `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/src/components/badge.css` lines 1-35 (the block), rules follow at line 36+.
- **`.ts`-inline-authored** — a `css`-tagged template literal in the `.ts` record, with `${p}` interpolating the prefix. Example: `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/src/components/button.ts` lines 10-42 (block inside `css\`` … at line 43 the `.${p}button {` rule starts). Note the mandatory `// prettier-ignore` on the line before the template (line 9).

The badge block (`badge.css:1-35`) is a good canonical example — it uses `@component`, `@summary`, many `@modifier`, `@pseudo`, `@cssproperty`, `@remarks`, `@animation`, `@example`, `@wrapper`, `@structure`, `@related`, `@demo`.

**Record kinds** (the opening tag, one per block): `@component`, `@utility`, `@rule`, `@declaration`. Examples of each:
- `@component` — `button.ts:11`, `badge.css:2`
- `@utility` — `formats/components/src/utilities/spacing.ts:28`
- `@rule` — `formats/components/src/rules/prose.ts:16`
- `@declaration` — `formats/components/src/declarations/focus.ts:20` (the only one; see §3)

The single source of truth is **`@cssdoc/spec`** — `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/node_modules/.pnpm/@cssdoc+spec@0.7.8/node_modules/@cssdoc/spec/dist/index.mjs` (the `CSSDOC_TAGS` array). `@cssdoc/core` seeds its parser from it. Tags have a `kind` (`record` / `block` / `modifier` / `inline`), an optional `aliasFor`, and `allowMultiple`:

- **Record tags**: `component`, `utility`, `rule`, `declaration`, plus `name` (alt component opener).
- **Block tags** (single-use): `class`, `summary`, `remarks`, `privateRemarks`, `deprecated`, `since`, `group` (alias `category`), `defaultValue`, `structure`, `demo`, `usage`.

- **`undocumented-modifier`** — a `.-modifier` selector exists in the CSS but has no `@modifier` tag.

# CSS documentation + externalization sweep

## Context

`formats/components/src/{declarations,lib,rules,utilities}` and `plugins/pantoken/*` all emit CSS.
This sweep answers four questions about that surface: what needs a cssdoc block, what blocks are
incomplete, what inline template-literal CSS can be externalized to the `.css`-file model, and whether
`plugins/pantoken/stacking` is dead code. The exploration produced clear, sometimes surprising answers —
one premise (stacking is dead) is false, and the components package is already fully documented — so the
actual work concentrates on the plugins plus two small, high-value changes.

### What the sweep found (the answers)

- **Q4 — `plugins/pantoken/stacking` is NOT dead code.** It emits `z-index` tokens (`--instui-stacking-*`)
  and `.instui-stack-*` utility classes from InstUI's View stacking scale. `declarations/elevation` emits
  `box-shadow` tokens (`--instui-elevation-*`) — a different property, namespace, and concern. Stacking is
  fully wired: re-exported by the `@pantoken` aggregate (namespace + `./stacking` subpath), a dependency of
  `packages/pantoken` and `docs`, consumed by `docs/scripts/demos.ts` to emit `stacking.css`, and covered by
  its own tests. **No action — removing it would break the aggregate package.**
- **Q1/Q2 — Inside `formats/components`, cssdoc coverage is already complete and gate-enforced.** Every record
  carries a block; `@cssdoc/valid-doc-comments` (in the `ready` gate + CI over `generated/*.css` and the
  co-located source `.css`) enforces `@summary` and flags `undocumented-modifier`/`undocumented-part`. On this
  green branch there are no known-incomplete blocks in the validated set. The genuinely **undocumented,
  unvalidated** CSS is `plugins/pantoken/*` (see below) and the `elevation` helper.
- **Q3 — Only `rules/base.ts` is a clean externalization fit.** Everything else still holding inline `css\`\``
  is a parameterized generator (runtime color math, shared fragments, JS-loop-built rules) that cannot become
  static `.css` — which is exactly why the codegen `sources` is limited to `components/` + `utilities/`.

## Work items

### 1. Bring `plugins/pantoken/*` into cssdoc — docs + lint + API pages (full scope)

_(Filled in from the plugin-integration design — see section below once the Plan agent returns.)_

### 2. Promote `elevation` to a documented `@declaration` record

Mirror the `focus` declaration exactly. `declarations/focus.ts` is the template: a static `FOCUS_DOC` cssdoc
block (`css\`/** @declaration focus ... */\``), a bespoke builder that prepends it, and a `Definition`-shaped
object registered in `DECLARATIONS`.

- **`formats/components/src/declarations/elevation.ts`**
  - Add an `ELEVATION_DOC` `css\`\`` block: `@declaration elevation`, `@summary`, one `@cssproperty
    --instui-elevation-<name>` per level/alias (resting, above, topmost, depth1–3, card, cardHover),
    `@related view` (the `view -shadow-*` modifiers consume it), `@demo self:elevation` (the
    `docs/demos/elevation.html` demo already exists), and an `@a11y`/`@remarks` note if useful.
  - Prepend `ELEVATION_DOC` in `elevationCss()` output (as `focusOutlineCss` prepends `FOCUS_DOC`), so the
    block leads `components.css` and flows into lint + `build-css-api`. Keep the `selector` option working.
  - Add a `Definition`-shaped `elevation` export (`kind: "declaration"`, `rules`/`css` delegating to
    `elevationCss()`), like `focus` at the bottom of `focus.ts`.
- **`formats/components/src/declarations/index.ts`** — add `elevation` to `DECLARATIONS` (`[focus, elevation]`)
  and update the module comment (it currently says elevation is "deliberately excluded").
- **`formats/components/tests/parity.test.ts:20`** — `DECLARATIONS.length` `1` → `2`.
- Token drift is already handled: `tests/_validate.ts:20-21` treats `--instui-elevation-*` as local, and
  `build-css-api.ts` already indexes elevation shadows as local vars + has an `elevation` `PROPERTY_SYNTAX`
  entry, so the API page resolves values automatically once the record tag exists.
- **Guide:** note the new declaration in `docs/guide/components.md` (the elevation shadows are already
  described around line 163) if a declarations list exists there.

### 3. Externalize `rules/base.ts` to the `.css` model

`base.ts`'s body is fully static (no `${}` interpolation, no prefix) — the one file that maps exactly onto the
`components/`+`utilities/` `.css`-file model.

- **New `formats/components/src/rules/base.css`** — the `/** @rule base ... */` doc block + the `*`/`html`/
  `body`/`a`/`::selection` rules, verbatim from `base.ts` (real CSS: literal backticks, no `\`` escaping, no
  `pfx-` sentinel since base uses no prefix).
- **`formats/components/scripts/component-styles.ts`** — add `join(srcDir, "rules")` to the `sources` array so
  the codegen picks up `base.css` → `generated/component-styles.ts` const `base`. (`prose.css` doesn't exist,
  so prose stays `.ts`; only `base.css` is scanned.)
- **`formats/components/src/rules/base.ts`** — reduce to the thin wrapper: import `base as baseRaw` from
  `../generated/component-styles.ts`, `export const base = defineRule({ name: "base", css: () => baseRaw })`,
  keep `export const baseRuleCss = base.css`. No `replaceAll(SENTINEL, …)` — base has no sentinel.
- **`vite.config.ts`** `lint:css`/`lint:js` globs — extend
  `formats/components/src/{components,utilities}/*.css` to `{components,utilities,rules}/*.css` so the new
  source `base.css` is linted like the other source records.
- Output must stay byte-identical: `generate.ts:109` still calls `baseCss()`; `define.ts` normalizes
  whitespace. The `sheets`/parity tests will catch any drift.

## Verification

- `pnpm run ready` — the full gate (`build:all` → `check:all`, `test:all`, `lint:css`, `lint:js`,
  `validate:generated:only`, `lint:markdown`). Must pass. This runs the cssdoc linter over the new plugin
  sheets + `base.css`, the parity test (elevation now = 2 declarations), and regenerates the sheets.
- `pnpm run check:publish` — publish gate, since plugin manifests/exports may change.
- Build the docs CSS-API locally and confirm new pages render: run the `docs:api` chain (TypeDoc →
  `build-css-api.ts`) and check `docs/api/css/` for `elevation` and the plugin records, then browser-verify a
  page (elevation shadows, `.instui-stack-*`, `.instui-transition`) via the preview server on a distinct
  `--strictPort` port.
- Spot-check that `generated/base.css` and `generated/components.css` (elevation block) are unchanged except
  for the intended doc-block addition (`git diff` the generated sheets after `build:all`).

## Notes / decisions locked with the user

- Plugin docs: **full** — cssdoc blocks + lint enforcement + CSS-API pages.
- Elevation: **promote** to `@declaration`.
- Externalization: **`base.ts` only** — the parameterized generators stay `.ts` by design.

# Design: bring `plugins/pantoken/*` CSS into the cssdoc system

## What I verified

**The proven pattern already exists in-repo.** `formats/components/scripts/generate.ts` (lines 134-147) authors a cssdoc block for a *generated* utility whose emitted classes are `.instui-*`, not `pfx-`:

```
/**
 * @utility color
 * @class .instui-text-danger
 * @summary Semantic colour utilities: `.instui-bg-<name>`, ...
 * @example <p class="instui-text-danger">...</p>
 */
```

It prepends this to `colorUtilitiesCss(...)` and writes the whole thing into `generated/utilities.css`. That single record:
- lint-validates because `generated/*.css` is in the `lint:css`/`lint:js` globs (root `vite.config.ts` lines 77, 82),
- feeds `build-css-api.ts` because it reads `formats/components/generated/utilities.css`,
- covers *hundreds* of sibling `.instui-bg-*`/`.instui-text-*`/`.instui-stroke-*` classes under one `@utility` record, with `@class` naming a representative.

This resolves the two hardest questions up front:
- **The SENTINEL/prefix problem is a non-issue.** Plugin sheets are emitted at the fixed `instui` prefix and never re-prefixed by a consumer's `raw.replaceAll(SENTINEL, p)`, so they carry no `pfx-` sentinel. cssdoc associates the doc comment with the immediately-following rules and uses `@class` to name the canonical selector — exactly as the `color` utility does. No sentinel needed.
- **`@utility` + `@class` is the record kind.** The RECORD regex in `build-css-api.ts` (`@(?:component|utility|rule|declaration)`, lines 155, 181) and the shipping `color` record both confirm `@utility` parses and renders today.

**Gitignore reality (important for ordering):** `.gitignore` ignores `**/generated/`. NONE of the generated sheets are committed — `formats/components/generated/*.css` and the existing `plugins/pantoken/{logos,primitives}/generated/*.css` are all reproduced by `vp run -r build` (the `build:all` node). So `build-css-api` already depends on `build:all` having run first (true in CI; `docs:dev` additionally runs `@pantoken/components#generate`). Plugin sheets slot into this exact model.

**Two plugin shapes:**
- `logos`, `primitives` already have `scripts/generate.ts` + committed-shape `generated/*.css` + a static `./x.css` export + are already in `tools/validate-generated/index.ts`. They only lack a cssdoc block.
- `stacking`, `transition`, `visual-debug` build rules inline in JS, have no generate script, no generated sheet, and export only `.` — they need the full generate/pack/export scaffold (mirroring `primitives`).

## Design decisions

1. **Where the doc block lives:** author it in each plugin's `scripts/generate.ts` (not in `src/index.ts`), so it never bloats the runtime `toCss` output — matching the `color` precedent. `generate.ts` composes `:root{declarations}` + doc block + rules and writes `generated/<name>.css`. The doc block must sit *immediately before* the class rules (cssdoc binds a comment to the next rule), so the `:root` declarations block goes *first*, then doc, then the `.instui-*` rules.

2. **Node-free constraint respected:** the doc/composition logic lives in `scripts/generate.ts` (a build script, not in `files`), which may use `node:fs` — exactly as `logos`/`primitives` already do. `src/index.ts` stays Node-free. To let `generate.ts` compose without duplicating the rules, export the module-level `rules` string (and a small declarations accessor) from each plugin `src/index.ts` — these are plain strings, still Node-free.

3. **Feeding `build-css-api.ts`: a second `emitCssApi` call.** `emitCssApi`'s `mergeCssSidebar` *replaces the section with the same label* and preserves others, so a second call with a distinct `label` (e.g. `"CSS plugins"`) and its own `outSubdir`/`baseHref` cleanly appends a second section while keeping the existing `"CSS"` section. A second call is preferable to extending the single `css[]` array because every plugin-specific hook diverges from the component path:
   - `importSnippet` must emit `@import "@pantoken/plugin-stacking/stacking.css";`, not `@pantoken/components/...`,
   - `resolveSource` must point at the plugin's `scripts/generate.ts` (its own `sourceMap`),
   - `resolveToken`/`localVars` must be rebuilt from the plugin sheets so `--instui-stacking-*` and `--instui-transition-*` resolve (they're defined in each sheet's `:root`, so the existing `matchAll(/(--[\w-]+)\s*:\s*.../)` localVars scan picks them up once the plugin sheets are in the scanned string),
   - the drift guard `unknownReferences(css, tokens)` (lines 269-274) would flag `--instui-stacking-*`, `--instui-transition-*`, `--pantoken-visual-debug-color` — a second call keeps that guard scoped to component sheets only, avoiding widening the allow-filter.

   (Alternative if a *unified* "CSS" section is wanted: keep one call, add plugin sheets to `sheets`/`cssPaths`, add a name→package map for `importSnippet`, include plugin generate scripts in `componentSources`, and extend the drift-guard prefix filter to allow `--instui-stacking-`, `--instui-transition-`, `--pantoken-`. More branching, one section.)

4. **Lint globs:** add `"plugins/pantoken/*/generated/*.css"` to both `lint:css` and `lint:js` in root `vite.config.ts` (lines 76-83). Both tasks already `dependsOn: ["build:all"]`, and each plugin's `build` will run its `generate` (see below), so the sheets exist before lint runs — same "generate exactly once through build:all" guarantee noted in that file. No new race.

## Ordered implementation plan

**A. Runtime-only plugins (`stacking`, `transition`, `visual-debug`) — add the generate scaffold**

1. `plugins/pantoken/{stacking,transition,visual-debug}/src/index.ts` — export the rules string (already module-level in `stacking`/`transition`; `visual-debug` builds `rules` from the default color — export a `visualDebugRules` const or a zero-arg helper). Keep Node-free.
2. New `plugins/pantoken/{stacking,transition,visual-debug}/scripts/generate.ts` — compose `:root { <declarations> }` (resolved via the plugin's `definitions`/`declarations`, or `toCss([], { plugins:[x()] })` split so the `:root` block leads) + the authored cssdoc `/** @utility <name> @class .instui-... @summary ... @modifier ... @example ... */` + the rules, then `writeFileSync(generated/<name>.css)`. Model file: `plugins/pantoken/primitives/scripts/generate.ts`. Transition needs one `@modifier` line per state class (`-fade-entering`, `-scale-exiting`, `-slide-*`, …) or the `undocumented-modifier` rule trips; visual-debug is `@utility visual-debug` + `@class .-with-visual-debug`.
3. `plugins/pantoken/{stacking,transition,visual-debug}/vite.config.ts` — add the `build` task `["vp run generate","vp pack"]`, a `generate` task, and a `pack.entry` for `generated/<name>.css`, mirroring `plugins/pantoken/primitives/vite.config.ts`.
4. `plugins/pantoken/{stacking,transition,visual-debug}/package.json` — add `"generate": "node scripts/generate.ts"` and a static `"./<name>.css": "./dist/<name>.css"` export (mirror `primitives`).

**B. Already-generated plugins (`logos`, `primitives`) — add the doc block only**

5. `plugins/pantoken/logos/scripts/generate.ts` and `plugins/pantoken/primitives/scripts/generate.ts` — prepend a `@utility` doc block (with a representative `@class`, e.g. `.instui-bg-primitive-color-aurora-aurora10` for primitives) to the emitted sheet before writing. No new export/task needed — they already ship the sheet and are in `validate-generated`.

**C. Lint**

6. Root `vite.config.ts` — add `"plugins/pantoken/*/generated/*.css"` to the `stylelint` (`lint:css`) and `eslint` (`lint:js`) glob lists.

**D. Docs CSS-API**

7. `docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts` — add a second `emitCssApi` call after the existing one, reading `plugins/pantoken/{stacking,transition,visual-debug,logos,primitives}/generated/*.css`, with `label:"CSS plugins"`, its own `resolveSource` (sourceMap over the plugin `scripts/generate.ts` files), `importSnippet` (`@import "@pantoken/plugin-<x>/<x>.css";`), and a `resolveToken` whose `localVars` are rebuilt from the plugin sheets. Keep the component drift guard scoped to the component `css` string only. Run the plugin call *after* the component call so its `mergeCssSidebar` preserves the existing `"CSS"` section.

**E. Drift guard / build ordering**

8. `tools/validate-generated/index.ts` — add `plugins/pantoken/{stacking,transition,visual-debug}` to `GENERATOR_PKGS` (non-empty `generated/`) and `FINALIZED_CSS_PKGS` (their new `./x.css` dist export), and add the `stacking`/`transition` (self-defining) sheets to `SELF_CONTAINED` for the dangling-ref check. Verify `visual-debug`'s `--pantoken-visual-debug-color` (a var *with* an inline fallback, defined nowhere) doesn't trip `danglingReferences` — if it does, that sheet stays out of `SELF_CONTAINED` or the fallback var is exempted.
9. `docs/package.json` `docs:dev` — it runs `@pantoken/components#generate` before `docs:api:css` but not the plugins'. In CI (`docs:build` → `build-api-locales.ts`) the plugin sheets come from `build:all`, so CI is fine; for `docs:dev` freshness, add the three plugin `#generate` runs (or rely on a prior `build:all`). This is orchestration only — do NOT make `build-css-api.ts` spawn `vp run` (the nested-vp-spawn limitation): it must stay a pure file reader.

**F. Optional DRY**

10. `docs/scripts/demos.ts` (lines 82-94) currently regenerates `stacking.css`/`transition.css`/`visual-debug.css` into `public/demos-assets/` in-process via `toCss` (no doc comments — fine for painting). Optionally switch these to `copyFileSync(require.resolve("@pantoken/plugin-<x>/<x>.css"), ...)` to reuse the new generated sheets. Not load-bearing; leave as-is for a minimal change.

## Risks / gotchas

- **Doc-comment adjacency:** cssdoc binds the comment to the *next* rule. Emit the `:root{}` declarations first, then the doc block immediately before the `.instui-*` class rules — otherwise the record attaches to `:root` and validation/rendering break.
- **`undocumented-modifier` volume:** `transition` has ~14 state classes; every `-fade-*`/`-scale-*`/`-slide-*` modifier must be listed as `@modifier` or the lint rule fails. `stacking`'s four `.instui-stack-<level>` are sibling utility classes (not modifiers) under one `@utility` record — the `color` utility proves cssdoc tolerates many pattern-siblings with one `@class`.
- **Token resolution:** `--instui-stacking-*`/`--instui-transition-*` must be present in the plugin sheet's `:root` for `resolveToken`'s `localVars` scan to resolve them in the "Tokens consumed" table; ensure `generate.ts` includes the declarations block. `--pantoken-visual-debug-color` has an inline fallback and no IR/token entry — `resolveToken` returns undefined (acceptable), but confirm the two drift guards (`build-css-api` and `validate-generated`) don't flag it.
- **Ordering:** plugin `generated/*.css` is gitignored and must be produced by `build:all` before `lint:css`/`lint:js` and before `build-css-api`. The new per-plugin `build` task (`vp run generate` → `vp pack`) plus the existing `dependsOn:["build:all"]` on the lint tasks preserves the "generate exactly once" guarantee — no concurrent writes to the same `generated/` dir.
- **`validate-generated` gates:** adding a `./x.css` export without adding the package to `FINALIZED_CSS_PKGS`/`GENERATOR_PKGS` will fail the guard (or silently skip); keep them in sync.
- **Browser Node-free constraint:** all `node:fs` stays in `scripts/generate.ts`; only plain strings are exported from `src/index.ts`.

### Critical Files for Implementation
- /Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts
- /Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/components/scripts/generate.ts (the `@utility color` + `@class` reference pattern to copy)
- /Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/plugins/pantoken/primitives/scripts/generate.ts and /Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/plugins/pantoken/primitives/vite.config.ts (scaffold to mirror for stacking/transition/visual-debug)
- /Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/vite.config.ts (lint:css / lint:js globs)
- /Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/tools/validate-generated/index.ts (GENERATOR_PKGS / FINALIZED_CSS_PKGS / SELF_CONTAINED)</result>

# CSS documentation + externalization sweep

## Context

`formats/components/src/{declarations,lib,rules,utilities}` and `plugins/pantoken/*` all emit CSS.
This sweep answers four questions about that surface: what needs a cssdoc block, what blocks are
incomplete, what inline template-literal CSS can be externalized to the `.css`-file model, and whether
`plugins/pantoken/stacking` is dead code. The exploration produced clear, sometimes surprising answers —
one premise (stacking is dead) is false, and the components package is already fully documented — so the
actual work concentrates on the plugins plus two small, high-value changes.

### What the sweep found (the answers)

- **Q4 — `plugins/pantoken/stacking` is NOT dead code.** It emits `z-index` tokens (`--instui-stacking-*`)
  and `.instui-stack-*` utility classes from InstUI's View stacking scale. `declarations/elevation` emits
  `box-shadow` tokens (`--instui-elevation-*`) — a different property, namespace, and concern. Stacking is
  fully wired: re-exported by the `@pantoken` aggregate (namespace + `./stacking` subpath), a dependency of
  `packages/pantoken` and `docs`, consumed by `docs/scripts/demos.ts` to emit `stacking.css`, and covered by
  its own tests. **No action — removing it would break the aggregate package.**
- **Q1/Q2 — Inside `formats/components`, cssdoc coverage is already complete and gate-enforced.** Every record
  carries a block; `@cssdoc/valid-doc-comments` (in the `ready` gate + CI over `generated/*.css` and the
  co-located source `.css`) enforces `@summary` and flags `undocumented-modifier`/`undocumented-part`. On this
  green branch there are no known-incomplete blocks in the validated set. The genuinely **undocumented,
  unvalidated** CSS is `plugins/pantoken/*` (see below) and the `elevation` helper.
- **Q3 — Only `rules/base.ts` is a clean externalization fit.** Everything else still holding inline `css\`\``
  is a parameterized generator (runtime color math, shared fragments, JS-loop-built rules) that cannot become
  static `.css` — which is exactly why the codegen `sources` is limited to `components/` + `utilities/`.

## Work items

### 1. Bring `plugins/pantoken/*` into cssdoc — docs + lint + API pages (full scope)

_(Filled in from the plugin-integration design — see section below once the Plan agent returns.)_

### 2. Promote `elevation` to a documented `@declaration` record

Mirror the `focus` declaration exactly. `declarations/focus.ts` is the template: a static `FOCUS_DOC` cssdoc
block (`css\`/** @declaration focus ... */\``), a bespoke builder that prepends it, and a `Definition`-shaped
object registered in `DECLARATIONS`.

- **`formats/components/src/declarations/elevation.ts`**
  - Add an `ELEVATION_DOC` `css\`\`` block: `@declaration elevation`, `@summary`, one `@cssproperty
    --instui-elevation-<name>` per level/alias (resting, above, topmost, depth1–3, card, cardHover),
    `@related view` (the `view -shadow-*` modifiers consume it), `@demo self:elevation` (the
    `docs/demos/elevation.html` demo already exists), and an `@a11y`/`@remarks` note if useful.
  - Prepend `ELEVATION_DOC` in `elevationCss()` output (as `focusOutlineCss` prepends `FOCUS_DOC`), so the
    block leads `components.css` and flows into lint + `build-css-api`. Keep the `selector` option working.
  - Add a `Definition`-shaped `elevation` export (`kind: "declaration"`, `rules`/`css` delegating to
    `elevationCss()`), like `focus` at the bottom of `focus.ts`.
- **`formats/components/src/declarations/index.ts`** — add `elevation` to `DECLARATIONS` (`[focus, elevation]`)
  and update the module comment (it currently says elevation is "deliberately excluded").
- **`formats/components/tests/parity.test.ts:20`** — `DECLARATIONS.length` `1` → `2`.
- Token drift is already handled: `tests/_validate.ts:20-21` treats `--instui-elevation-*` as local, and
  `build-css-api.ts` already indexes elevation shadows as local vars + has an `elevation` `PROPERTY_SYNTAX`
  entry, so the API page resolves values automatically once the record tag exists.
- **Guide:** note the new declaration in `docs/guide/components.md` (the elevation shadows are already
  described around line 163) if a declarations list exists there.

### 3. Externalize `rules/base.ts` to the `.css` model

`base.ts`'s body is fully static (no `${}` interpolation, no prefix) — the one file that maps exactly onto the
`components/`+`utilities/` `.css`-file model.

- **New `formats/components/src/rules/base.css`** — the `/** @rule base ... */` doc block + the `*`/`html`/
  `body`/`a`/`::selection` rules, verbatim from `base.ts` (real CSS: literal backticks, no `\`` escaping, no
  `pfx-` sentinel since base uses no prefix).
- **`formats/components/scripts/component-styles.ts`** — add `join(srcDir, "rules")` to the `sources` array so
  the codegen picks up `base.css` → `generated/component-styles.ts` const `base`. (`prose.css` doesn't exist,
  so prose stays `.ts`; only `base.css` is scanned.)
- **`formats/components/src/rules/base.ts`** — reduce to the thin wrapper: import `base as baseRaw` from
  `../generated/component-styles.ts`, `export const base = defineRule({ name: "base", css: () => baseRaw })`,
  keep `export const baseRuleCss = base.css`. No `replaceAll(SENTINEL, …)` — base has no sentinel.
- **`vite.config.ts`** `lint:css`/`lint:js` globs — extend
  `formats/components/src/{components,utilities}/*.css` to `{components,utilities,rules}/*.css` so the new
  source `base.css` is linted like the other source records.
- Output must stay byte-identical: `generate.ts:109` still calls `baseCss()`; `define.ts` normalizes
  whitespace. The `sheets`/parity tests will catch any drift.

## Verification

- `pnpm run ready` — the full gate (`build:all` → `check:all`, `test:all`, `lint:css`, `lint:js`,
  `validate:generated:only`, `lint:markdown`). Must pass. This runs the cssdoc linter over the new plugin
  sheets + `base.css`, the parity test (elevation now = 2 declarations), and regenerates the sheets.
- `pnpm run check:publish` — publish gate, since plugin manifests/exports may change.
- Build the docs CSS-API locally and confirm new pages render: run the `docs:api` chain (TypeDoc →
  `build-css-api.ts`) and check `docs/api/css/` for `elevation` and the plugin records, then browser-verify a
  page (elevation shadows, `.instui-stack-*`, `.instui-transition`) via the preview server on a distinct
  `--strictPort` port.
- Spot-check that `generated/base.css` and `generated/components.css` (elevation block) are unchanged except
  for the intended doc-block addition (`git diff` the generated sheets after `build:all`).

## Notes / decisions locked with the user

- Plugin docs: **full** — cssdoc blocks + lint enforcement + CSS-API pages.
- Elevation: **promote** to `@declaration`.
- Externalization: **`base.ts` only** — the parameterized generators stay `.ts` by design.
