# cssdoc grouping & `@group` investigation (v0.7.8)

All packages resolve to `@cssdoc/*@0.7.8`. pantoken's `docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts` imports `emitCssApi` from `@cssdoc/typedoc`, `parseCssDocs` + `CssDocEntry` from `@cssdoc/core`, and `CssDocConfigFile` from `@cssdoc/config`. Types ship in each package's `dist/index.d.mts`; the runtime `dist/index.mjs` files are **formatted (not minified)** and readable.

---

## 1. `KIND_GROUPS` and the two functions that consume it

**File:** `node_modules/.pnpm/@cssdoc+markdown@0.7.8/node_modules/@cssdoc/markdown/dist/index.mjs`

`KIND_GROUPS` (lines 31–49) — display order is fixed: component, utility, rule, declaration.

```js
/** Sidebar/index groups, in display order. Only kinds with records appear. */
const KIND_GROUPS = [
  { kind: "component",   label: "Components" },
  { kind: "utility",     label: "Utilities" },
  { kind: "rule",        label: "Rules" },
  { kind: "declaration", label: "Declarations" },
];
```

It is consumed by exactly two exported functions. **The grouping key is `record.kind` in both** — never `group`/`category`.

**(a) Index-page groups — `renderIndex`** (index.mjs lines 305–323):

```js
function renderIndex(entries, options = {}) {
  const baseHref = options.baseHref ?? "/";
  const lines = [`# ${options.title ?? "CSS API reference"}`, ""];
  if (options.intro) lines.push(escProse(options.intro), "");
  for (const group of KIND_GROUPS) {
    const inGroup = entries.filter((e) => e.kind === group.kind);
    if (!inGroup.length) continue;                    // empty groups dropped
    lines.push(`## ${group.label}`, "", ...table(
      ["Name", "Class", "Summary"],
      inGroup.map((e) => [
        `[${e.name}](${baseHref}${e.name}.md)`,
        `\`${e.className}\``,
        cell(e.summary),
      ])));
  }
  return `${lines.join("\n")}\n`;
}
```

**(b) Sidebar groups — `buildSidebar`** (index.mjs lines 334–351):

```js
/** Build the sidebar tree (Overview, then a group per kind). */
function buildSidebar(entries, baseHref = "/") {
  const sidebar = [{ text: "Overview", link: baseHref }];
  for (const group of KIND_GROUPS) {
    const items = entries.filter((e) => e.kind === group.kind).map((e) => ({
      text: e.name,
      link: `${baseHref}${e.name}.md`,
    }));
    if (items.length) sidebar.push({ text: group.label, collapsed: false, items });  // empty groups dropped
  }
  return sidebar;
}
```

**Signatures** (from `dist/index.d.mts` lines 148–149, 102–103):

```ts
declare function buildSidebar(entries: readonly CssDocEntry[], baseHref?: string): SidebarItem[];
declare function renderIndex(entries: readonly CssDocEntry[], options?: RenderIndexOptions): string;
```

`SidebarItem` (index.d.mts 107–112): `{ text: string; link?: string; collapsed?: boolean; items?: SidebarItem[] }`.

**Grouping logic summary:** both functions iterate `KIND_GROUPS` in its fixed array order; for each group they `entries.filter(e => e.kind === group.kind)`; a group producing zero records is skipped (`continue` in renderIndex, `if (items.length)` in buildSidebar). No sort within a group (entries arrive already sorted by name — see `BuildCssApiResult.entries` "sorted by name", index.d.mts line 140). Group order and labels are hard-coded in `KIND_GROUPS`; there is no option to reorder or relabel them.

---

## 2. The `@group` / `@category` tag — definition and current use

**Definition — `@cssdoc/spec`**, `dist/index.mjs` lines 71–79 (inside `CSSDOC_TAGS`):

```js
{ name: "group",    kind: "block" },
{ name: "category", kind: "block", aliasFor: "group" },
```

So `group` is a **block** tag, single-valued (no `allowMultiple`), and `category` is a straight alias of it. The `CssdocTag` shape is in spec's `index.d.mts` (lines 24–37). Mirror definitions/derivations:
- `@cssdoc/core` `ParsedDoc.group` — `dist/lite-CLGf1QSF.d.mts` line 698: `/** @group/@category — a documentation group. */ group?: string;`
- `CssDocEntry.group` — same file, line 454: `/** A documentation group/category, from @group/@category. */ group?: string;`

**Is it rendered / used?** — **Not a pure no-op, but it does NOT drive sidebar or index grouping.** A grep of the markdown runtime for `.group` finds exactly one consumer: the per-page **meta line** in `renderEntry`.

`@cssdoc/markdown/dist/index.mjs` lines 152–157:

```js
const meta = [];
if (entry.since)  meta.push(`**Since:** ${escProse(entry.since)}`);
if (entry.group)  meta.push(`**Group:** ${escProse(entry.group)}`);          // <-- the only use
const src = options.resolveSource?.(entry);
if (src) meta.push(`**Source:** [${escProse(src.label ?? "source")}](${src.href})`);
if (meta.length) lines.push(meta.join(" · "), "");
```

So `entry.group` renders as a `**Group:** <value>` fragment on the fixed header meta line (joined with Since/Source by ` · `). It is **display-only metadata**: it does not feed `buildSidebar`, `renderIndex`, `buildCssApi`, or any sidebar/section grouping. Sidebar and index grouping are driven solely by `record.kind`. (The `RenderEntryOptions` doc comment confirms this — index.d.mts lines 20–23 describe "the Since/Group/Source meta line" as part of the fixed page header.)

Implication for the proposal: `@group`/`@category` is currently free to repurpose for sidebar/index grouping — its only existing behavior is the one-line meta string, which a grouping feature could either keep, subsume, or supersede.

---

## 3. `CssDocEntry` (record type) — full shape

**File:** `@cssdoc/core/dist/lite-CLGf1QSF.d.mts` lines 436–516. Grouping-relevant fields highlighted (`name`, `kind`, `className`, `group`, `releaseStage`):

```ts
/** One documented CSS record: its base class plus everything derived from the CSS + doc comments. */
interface CssDocEntry {
  /** The record name from @component/@utility/@rule/@declaration/@name, e.g. `button`. */
  name: string;
  /** Which kind of CSS surface this documents (defaults to `component`). */
  kind: CssRecordKind;
  /** The base class selector, e.g. `.button` (inferred from the first bare-class rule). */
  className: string;
  /** One-line summary from @summary. */
  summary?: string;
  /** Extended prose from @remarks. */
  remarks?: string;
  /** Internal-only prose from @privateRemarks (emitters may choose to omit it from public output). */
  privateRemarks?: string;
  /** The release stage from a modifier flag tag (@alpha/@beta/@experimental/@internal/@public). */
  releaseStage?: CssReleaseStage;
  /** Version introduced, from @since. */
  since?: string;
  /** A documentation group/category, from @group/@category. */
  group?: string;
  /** Accessibility guidance, from @a11y/@accessibility. */
  accessibility?: string;
  modifiers: CssModifier[];
  parts: CssPart[];
  shadowParts: CssPart[];
  pseudoElements: CssPseudoElement[];
  states: CssState[];
  slots: CssSlot[];
  todos: string[];
  cssPropertiesConsumed: CssTokenConsumed[];
  cssPropertiesDeclared: CssPropertyDeclared[];
  functions: CssFunction[];
  animations: CssAnimation[];
  layers: CssLayer[];
  conditions: CssCondition[];
  examples: string[];
  structure?: StructureNode[];
  structureDescription?: string;
  demo?: string;
  deprecated?: string;
  see: string[];
  usage?: string;
  compat: string[];
  related: CssRelated[];
  source?: CssSource;
  /** Content of registered custom (block) tags, keyed by tag name without its `@`. Absent when none found. */
  customBlocks?: Record<string, string[]>;
}
```

Supporting types (same file):
```ts
type CssRecordKind = "component" | "utility" | "rule" | "declaration";               // line 381
type CssReleaseStage = "alpha" | "beta" | "experimental" | "internal" | "public";     // line 386
```

So the record exposes `kind` (the current grouping key), `name`, and `group` (currently meta-only) but **no** dedicated group-order/group-label field. `customBlocks` is the one open-ended metadata escape hatch.

---

## 4. `emitCssApi` options + `mergeCssSidebar`

**File:** `@cssdoc/typedoc/dist/index.d.mts`. The options interface is named **`EmitCssApiOptions`** and `extends RenderEntryOptions` (so it inherits `resolveToken`, `resolveDemo`, `resolveSource`, `importSnippet`, `baseHref`, `resolveComponent`, `sectionOrder`, `headingPrefix`, `structureView`, `classNames`). Lines 10–32:

```ts
/** Options for {@link emitCssApi}. */
interface EmitCssApiOptions extends RenderEntryOptions {
  /** The TypeDoc output root (where `typedoc-sidebar.json` lives). */
  outputDirectory: string;
  /** CSS source file paths (resolved against `cwd`). */
  css: string[];
  /** Subdirectory under the output root for the CSS pages (default `"css"`). */
  outSubdir?: string;
  /** The sidebar section label (default `"CSS"`). */
  label?: string;
  /** Link prefix for the emitted pages/sidebar (default `"<outSubdir>/"`). */
  baseHref?: string;
  /** The tag configuration to parse with. */
  configuration?: CssDocConfiguration;
  /**
   * A loaded `cssdoc.json` (from @cssdoc/config). When given, it supplies the parse `configuration`
   * (unless one is passed explicitly) and the render defaults
   * sectionOrder/headingPrefix/baseHref/structureView from its `render` block. Any explicit
   * option above still overrides the config file.
   */
  configFile?: CssDocConfigFile;
  /** Base directory the `css` paths are resolved against (default `process.cwd()`). */
  cwd?: string;
}
```

Return type (index.d.mts 49–51): `BuildCssApiResult & { sidebarMerged: boolean }`. `BuildCssApiResult` (markdown index.d.mts 138–147): `{ entries: CssDocEntry[]; pages: string[]; indexPath: string; sidebarPath: string }`.

Note the classNames / resolveToken / resolveSource / importSnippet fields the user listed live on **`RenderEntryOptions`** (markdown `index.d.mts` lines 28–77), inherited here. No option relates to sidebar-group ordering or labels — only the single `label` for the top-level section.

**How the top-level section is built + merge semantics** — `@cssdoc/typedoc/dist/index.mjs`:

`emitCssApi` (lines 37–72) resolves `label = options.label ?? "CSS"`, calls `buildCssApi(...)` to write pages, then if `typedoc-sidebar.json` exists:

```js
const merged = mergeCssSidebar(
  JSON.parse(readFileSync(sidebarPath, "utf8")),
  label,
  buildSidebar(result.entries, baseHref)      // Overview + one group per kind (KIND_GROUPS)
);
writeFileSync(sidebarPath, `${JSON.stringify(merged, null, 2)}\n`);
```

`mergeCssSidebar` (lines 23–29) — **replace-by-label**, matching on the node's `text`:

```js
function mergeCssSidebar(existing, label, cssItems) {
  return [...existing.filter((item) => item.text !== label), {
    text: label,          // the top-level section node, labelled by `label`
    collapsed: false,
    items: cssItems,      // Overview + the per-kind child groups from buildSidebar
  }];
}
```

So the merge drops any existing top-level node whose `text` equals `label` and appends a fresh one. The section's **children are the kind groups** produced by `buildSidebar` (Overview node first, then Components/Utilities/Rules/Declarations, empty kinds omitted). This is exactly why pantoken's two `emitCssApi` calls (labels `"CSS"` and `"CSS plugins"`) coexist — different labels, so neither replaces the other. `render.baseHref`/`sectionOrder`/`headingPrefix`/`structureView` are pulled from `configFile.render` as fallbacks (lines 41–45), explicit options winning.

---

## 5. Render config (`@cssdoc/config`) — is there any group option?

**File:** `@cssdoc/config/dist/index.d.mts`. The `render` block type is **`RenderConfig`** (lines 16–22):

```ts
interface RenderConfig {
  sectionOrder?: readonly string[];
  headingPrefix?: string;
  baseHref?: string;
  /** Which Structure representation(s) to emit: "text", "diagram", or "both" (default). */
  structureView?: "text" | "diagram" | "both";
}
```

Exposed on the loaded config as `CssDocConfigFile.render: Readonly<RenderConfig>` (index.d.mts lines 80–85), merged across the `extends` chain.

The JSON Schema `render` object (`cssDocSchema`, index.d.mts lines 317–342) enumerates exactly the same four keys — `sectionOrder`, `headingPrefix`, `baseHref`, `structureView` — with `additionalProperties: false`. `sectionOrder` controls the reorderable **`##` sections within one record page** (keys from `SectionKey`), not sidebar groups.

**There is no existing option anywhere for sidebar groups, group ordering, or group labels.** The whole kind-grouping (`KIND_GROUPS`) is hard-coded in `@cssdoc/markdown`, and `additionalProperties: false` at both the top level and inside `render` means a new option would need a schema addition. This is the gap the proposal addresses.

---

## 6. Public API surface per package

All five packages export only `"."` (→ `dist/index.mjs`) plus `"./package.json"`; `@cssdoc/core` additionally exports `"./lite"` (→ `dist/lite.mjs`). Public symbols (from each `index.d.mts` export list):

- **`@cssdoc/spec`**: `CSSDOC_TAGS`, `CSSDOC_TAG_NAMES`, `cssdocTagNamesByKind`, `cssdocTagNamesByArgument`; types `CssdocTag`, `CssdocTagKind`, `CssdocRecordKind`, `CssdocTagArgument`.

- **`@cssdoc/core`**: `parseCssDocs`, `parseDocComment`, `parseStructure`, `recordNameOf`, `stripCommentFraming`, `toJson`, `toMermaid`, `resolveModifierConvention`, classes `CssDocConfiguration`, `CssDocTagDefinition`, `ModifierMatcher`, consts `RECORD_TAGS`, `MODIFIER_PRESETS`, `DEFAULT_MODIFIER_CONVENTION`, `DEFAULT_PSEUDO_ELEMENTS`, `DEFAULT_STATE_PSEUDO_CLASSES`; types including `CssDocEntry`, `CssRecordKind`, `CssReleaseStage`, `ParseOptions`, `ParsedDoc`, `CssModifier`, `CssPart`, `CssState`, `StructureNode`, etc. (pantoken uses `parseCssDocs` + type `CssDocEntry`).

- **`@cssdoc/markdown`**: `buildCssApi`, `buildSidebar`, `renderEntry`, `renderIndex`, `cell`, `escProse`, `KIND_GROUPS`, `DEFAULT_SECTION_ORDER`; types `BuildCssApiOptions`, `BuildCssApiResult`, `RenderEntryOptions`, `RenderIndexOptions`, `SectionKey`, `SidebarItem`, `ResolveSource`, `ResolveToken`. (Note: `KIND_GROUPS` **is** a public export — but it's a `readonly` const array with no override hook.)

- **`@cssdoc/typedoc`**: `emitCssApi`, `mergeCssSidebar`, `load`, `TYPEDOC_SIDEBAR_FILE`; type `EmitCssApiOptions`. (pantoken uses `emitCssApi`.)

- **`@cssdoc/config`**: `CssDocConfigFile`, `resolveProviders`, `cssDocSchema`, `CSSDOC_CONFIG_FILENAME`, `CSSDOC_CONFIG_FILENAMES`; types `ProviderRef`, `ResolvedProviders` (and internal-but-exported-shape `RenderConfig`/`NamingOverride`/`RuleSeverityOverride` are referenced via `CssDocConfigFile` members, though only `ProviderRef`/`ResolvedProviders` are named in the export list — `RenderConfig` is reachable as the type of `CssDocConfigFile.render`). (pantoken uses `CssDocConfigFile`.)

---

## Proposal-relevant conclusions

# Proposal to send upstream to cssdoc: custom sidebar/index groups

## Context

pantoken's docs CSS-API (`docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts`) renders two `emitCssApi` sections —
`"CSS"` (components/utilities/rules/declarations) and `"CSS plugins"` (the plugin records). We want
the plugin records to appear **inside** the CSS section as a fifth subsection, so the CSS nav reads
`Components · Utilities · Rules · Declarations · Plugins`.

cssdoc can't express that today: sidebar/index grouping is hardcoded to the four record **kinds**, and
the only way to get a distinct plugin group is a second top-level `emitCssApi` section. The clean fix is
a small, general cssdoc feature — so **instead of post-processing pantoken's sidebar JSON, we send cssdoc
a proposal**. This plan's deliverable is that proposal document (below), ready to file as a cssdoc issue
/ discussion. pantoken adopts it once cssdoc ships (see "Follow-up").

- `KIND_GROUPS` in `@cssdoc/markdown/dist/index.mjs` — `[{kind:"component",label:"Components"}, {utility→Utilities}, {rule→Rules}, {declaration→Declarations}]`. `buildSidebar` and `renderIndex` group records solely by `record.kind` via the hardcoded `KIND_GROUPS`
array. A consumer that wants an extra section — e.g. a **Plugins** group holding records of mixed kinds
(some `@utility`, some `@declaration`) — has no supported way to do it within one section. The only
workarounds are:

1. A **second `emitCssApi` call** with a different `label` → a separate *top-level* sidebar section
   (`mergeCssSidebar` keys on `label`), which is a sibling of the main CSS section, not a child of it.
2. **Post-processing the emitted `typedoc-sidebar.json`** to splice the second section's items back in as
   a subgroup — brittle and outside cssdoc's contract.

pantoken hits exactly this: we document five CSS-emitting plugins (stacking/transition/visual-debug as
`@utility`, primitives as `@utility`, logos as `@declaration`) and want them under one **Plugins**
subsection of the CSS API, after Declarations. Today they land in a separate `"CSS plugins"` top-level
section.

- `@cssdoc/markdown` `KIND_GROUPS` = `component→Components`, `utility→Utilities`, `rule→Rules`,
  `declaration→Declarations` (fixed order).
- `buildSidebar(entries, baseHref)` and `renderIndex(entries, options)` both iterate `KIND_GROUPS`,
  `filter(e => e.kind === group.kind)`, and drop empty groups. Grouping key is `entry.kind` only.
- `@group`/`@category` is already parsed to `CssDocEntry.group?: string`, but only drives the per-page
  `**Group:** <value>` meta line in `renderEntry` — never the sidebar or index.

#### Proposed change

Group by **`entry.group ?? kindLabel(entry.kind)`** in both `buildSidebar` and `renderIndex`:

- A record **with** `@group Foo` joins a group labelled `Foo` (leaving its kind group).
- A record **without** `@group` stays in its kind group — unchanged.
- **Group order:** the kind groups first, in `KIND_GROUPS` order (each holding only its ungrouped
  records), then any custom `@group` groups in **first-appearance order** (deterministic — `entries`
  are already name-sorted). So `@group Plugins` records form a `Plugins` group after `Declarations` with
  zero extra config — which is exactly the pantoken layout.
- Empty groups are still dropped.

```js
// @cssdoc/markdown
function groupEntries(entries) {
  const kindLabel = Object.fromEntries(KIND_GROUPS.map(g => [g.kind, g.label]));
  const order = [];                    // group labels in display order
  const byLabel = new Map();           // label -> entries[]
  const push = (label, e) => {
    if (!byLabel.has(label)) { byLabel.set(label, []); }
    byLabel.get(label).push(e);
  };
  for (const g of KIND_GROUPS) order.push(g.label);          // kind groups first
  for (const e of entries) push(e.group ?? kindLabel[e.kind], e);
  for (const label of byLabel.keys())                        // then custom groups, first-appearance
    if (!order.includes(label)) order.push(label);
  return order.filter(l => byLabel.has(label => l)).map(label => ({ label, entries: byLabel.get(label) }));
}
```

`buildSidebar` and `renderIndex` then iterate `groupEntries(entries)` instead of `KIND_GROUPS`.

#### Optional: explicit group order

For consumers who want to pin or interleave order (e.g. put a custom group between kind groups, or
rename), add a `render.groups?: readonly string[]` to `RenderConfig` + `cssDocSchema` (mirroring the
existing `sectionOrder`), threaded through `EmitCssApiOptions` like `sectionOrder`/`structureView`
already are. Listed labels order first (in that order); unlisted groups append in the default order
above. Omitted → the default order. pantoken wouldn't need it (the default already yields
`…Declarations, Plugins`), but it makes the feature complete.

#### Backward compatibility

- Records without `@group` — **no change**.
- Records that already use `@group` today get sidebar/index grouping in addition to the existing
  `**Group:**` meta line. That's a behavior change for those records only. `@group` is niche and the new
  behavior is the tag's intuitive meaning, so we'd treat this as a minor release. If strict compatibility
  is preferred, gate it behind a `render.groupBy: "kind" | "group"` (default `"kind"`) — but we'd
  recommend making `@group` grouping the default.
- The per-page `**Group:** <value>` meta line can stay as-is (harmless) or be dropped once the group is
  visible in the nav — maintainers' call; not required by this proposal.

#### Consumer example (pantoken)

With this change, pantoken collapses its two `emitCssApi` calls into one and tags each plugin record:

```css

 * @utility stacking
 * @group Plugins
 * @summary z-index depth utilities…
 */
```

five plugin records (mixed kinds) under **Plugins**. No second section, no sidebar post-processing.

An emit-time option — `emitCssApi({ label: "CSS", group: "Plugins" })` that merges a call's records into

# Proposal to send upstream to cssdoc: custom sidebar/index groups

## Context

pantoken's docs CSS-API (`docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts`) renders two `emitCssApi` sections —
`"CSS"` (components/utilities/rules/declarations) and `"CSS plugins"` (the plugin records). We want
the plugin records to appear **inside** the CSS section as a fifth subsection, so the CSS nav reads
`Components · Utilities · Rules · Declarations · Plugins`.

cssdoc can't express that today: sidebar/index grouping is hardcoded to the four record **kinds**, and
the only way to get a distinct plugin group is a second top-level `emitCssApi` section. The clean fix is
a small, general cssdoc feature — so **instead of post-processing pantoken's sidebar JSON, we send cssdoc
a proposal**. This plan's deliverable is that proposal document (below), ready to file as a cssdoc issue
/ discussion. pantoken adopts it once cssdoc ships (see "Follow-up").

### Verified cssdoc internals (v0.7.8) the proposal builds on

- `KIND_GROUPS` in `@cssdoc/markdown/dist/index.mjs` — `[{kind:"component",label:"Components"}, {utility→Utilities}, {rule→Rules}, {declaration→Declarations}]`. Consumed **identically** by `buildSidebar` (sidebar tree) and `renderIndex` (index page) — both do `entries.filter(e => e.kind === group.kind)`, in fixed array order, dropping empty groups. No sort/label/order override.
- `@group`/`@category` — a `block` tag in `@cssdoc/spec` (`category` aliases `group`); parsed into `CssDocEntry.group?: string` in `@cssdoc/core`. **Currently used only** by `renderEntry` for the per-page `**Group:** <value>` meta line — it does NOT touch sidebar/index grouping. So it's free to repurpose.
- `EmitCssApiOptions` (`@cssdoc/typedoc`) extends `RenderEntryOptions`; `mergeCssSidebar(existing, label, cssItems)` replaces the top-level node whose `text === label`. `RenderConfig` (`@cssdoc/config`) = `sectionOrder`/`headingPrefix`/`baseHref`/`structureView`, `additionalProperties:false` (a new option needs a schema addition, mirroring how `sectionOrder`/`structureView` already thread through).
- Public symbols the proposal names: `buildSidebar`, `renderIndex`, `KIND_GROUPS` (`@cssdoc/markdown`); `emitCssApi`, `EmitCssApiOptions` (`@cssdoc/typedoc`); `RenderConfig`, `cssDocSchema` (`@cssdoc/config`); `CssDocEntry.group` (`@cssdoc/core`).

---

## Deliverable: the proposal document (ready to send)

> Save verbatim to `docs/internal/proposals/cssdoc-custom-groups.md` (new dir) and/or file it as an
> issue on the cssdoc repo. Written to cssdoc's maintainers, so it references their symbols directly.

---

### Proposal: group sidebar & index by `@group`, not only by record kind

**cssdoc version reviewed:** 0.7.8

#### Summary

Let CSS records opt into a named sidebar/index group via the existing `@group`/`@category` tag, instead
of always grouping by the four record kinds. Records without `@group` are unchanged. This is a small,
backward-compatible change in `@cssdoc/markdown`, and it removes the need for consumers to emit a second
top-level `emitCssApi` section (or post-process the sidebar) just to get a custom group.

#### Motivation

`buildSidebar` and `renderIndex` group records solely by `record.kind` via the hardcoded `KIND_GROUPS`
array. A consumer that wants an extra section — e.g. a **Plugins** group holding records of mixed kinds
(some `@utility`, some `@declaration`) — has no supported way to do it within one section. The only
workarounds are:

1. A **second `emitCssApi` call** with a different `label` → a separate *top-level* sidebar section
   (`mergeCssSidebar` keys on `label`), which is a sibling of the main CSS section, not a child of it.
2. **Post-processing the emitted `typedoc-sidebar.json`** to splice the second section's items back in as
   a subgroup — brittle and outside cssdoc's contract.

pantoken hits exactly this: we document five CSS-emitting plugins (stacking/transition/visual-debug as
`@utility`, primitives as `@utility`, logos as `@declaration`) and want them under one **Plugins**
subsection of the CSS API, after Declarations. Today they land in a separate `"CSS plugins"` top-level
section.

#### Current behavior (for reference)

- `@cssdoc/markdown` `KIND_GROUPS` = `component→Components`, `utility→Utilities`, `rule→Rules`,
  `declaration→Declarations` (fixed order).
- `buildSidebar(entries, baseHref)` and `renderIndex(entries, options)` both iterate `KIND_GROUPS`,
  `filter(e => e.kind === group.kind)`, and drop empty groups. Grouping key is `entry.kind` only.
- `@group`/`@category` is already parsed to `CssDocEntry.group?: string`, but only drives the per-page
  `**Group:** <value>` meta line in `renderEntry` — never the sidebar or index.

#### Proposed change

Group by **`entry.group ?? kindLabel(entry.kind)`** in both `buildSidebar` and `renderIndex`:

- A record **with** `@group Foo` joins a group labelled `Foo` (leaving its kind group).
- A record **without** `@group` stays in its kind group — unchanged.
- **Group order:** the kind groups first, in `KIND_GROUPS` order (each holding only its ungrouped
  records), then any custom `@group` groups in **first-appearance order** (deterministic — `entries`
  are already name-sorted). So `@group Plugins` records form a `Plugins` group after `Declarations` with
  zero extra config — which is exactly the pantoken layout.
- Empty groups are still dropped.

Sketch (shared helper so sidebar and index stay identical):

```js
// @cssdoc/markdown
function groupEntries(entries) {
  const kindLabel = Object.fromEntries(KIND_GROUPS.map(g => [g.kind, g.label]));
  const order = [];                    // group labels in display order
  const byLabel = new Map();           // label -> entries[]
  const push = (label, e) => {
    if (!byLabel.has(label)) { byLabel.set(label, []); }
    byLabel.get(label).push(e);
  };
  for (const g of KIND_GROUPS) order.push(g.label);          // kind groups first
  for (const e of entries) push(e.group ?? kindLabel[e.kind], e);
  for (const label of byLabel.keys())                        // then custom groups, first-appearance
    if (!order.includes(label)) order.push(label);
  return order.filter(l => byLabel.has(l)).map(l => ({ label: l, entries: byLabel.get(l) }));
}
```

`buildSidebar` and `renderIndex` then iterate `groupEntries(entries)` instead of `KIND_GROUPS`.

#### Optional: explicit group order

For consumers who want to pin or interleave order (e.g. put a custom group between kind groups, or
rename), add a `render.groups?: readonly string[]` to `RenderConfig` + `cssDocSchema` (mirroring the
existing `sectionOrder`), threaded through `EmitCssApiOptions` like `sectionOrder`/`structureView`
already are. Listed labels order first (in that order); unlisted groups append in the default order
above. Omitted → the default order. pantoken wouldn't need it (the default already yields
`…Declarations, Plugins`), but it makes the feature complete.

#### Backward compatibility

- Records without `@group` — **no change**.
- Records that already use `@group` today get sidebar/index grouping in addition to the existing
  `**Group:**` meta line. That's a behavior change for those records only. `@group` is niche and the new
  behavior is the tag's intuitive meaning, so we'd treat this as a minor release. If strict compatibility
  is preferred, gate it behind a `render.groupBy: "kind" | "group"` (default `"kind"`) — but we'd
  recommend making `@group` grouping the default.
- The per-page `**Group:** <value>` meta line can stay as-is (harmless) or be dropped once the group is
  visible in the nav — maintainers' call; not required by this proposal.

#### Consumer example (pantoken)

With this change, pantoken collapses its two `emitCssApi` calls into one and tags each plugin record:

```css
/**
 * @utility stacking
 * @group Plugins
 * @summary z-index depth utilities…
 */
```

Result: a single `"CSS"` section → `Components · Utilities · Rules · Declarations · Plugins`, with all
five plugin records (mixed kinds) under **Plugins**. No second section, no sidebar post-processing.

#### Alternative considered (and why we prefer the tag)

An emit-time option — `emitCssApi({ label: "CSS", group: "Plugins" })` that merges a call's records into
an existing section as one flat subgroup — would let a consumer keep separate `emitCssApi` calls (handy
when the groups need different `resolveSource`/`importSnippet`). But it changes `mergeCssSidebar` from
replace-by-label to merge-into-a-section, adds a "flat group" mode to `buildSidebar`, and is
per-call rather than per-record. The `@group` approach is smaller, reuses an existing tag and the
already-parsed `CssDocEntry.group`, and is authored where the record lives. We'd be happy with either;
the tag is our recommendation.

#### Touch points

- `@cssdoc/markdown`: `buildSidebar`, `renderIndex` (+ a shared `groupEntries` helper). Core change.
- `@cssdoc/config`: `RenderConfig` + `cssDocSchema` — only if the optional `render.groups` is adopted.
- `@cssdoc/typedoc`: thread `groups`/`groupBy` through `EmitCssApiOptions` → `buildCssApi`, alongside the
  existing `sectionOrder`/`structureView` defaults — only if the optional config is adopted.
- No change needed to `@cssdoc/core` (`CssDocEntry.group` already exists) or `@cssdoc/spec`.

---

## Follow-up (pantoken, after cssdoc ships)

Once cssdoc honors `@group` for grouping:

1. Add `@group Plugins` to the five plugin records (in each `plugins/pantoken/*/scripts/generate.ts` doc
   block: stacking, transition, visual-debug, primitives, logos).
2. Collapse the two `emitCssApi` calls in `docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts` into one — feed the plugin
   sheets into the `css` array, merge `resolveSource`/`importSnippet` into name-keyed maps (record names
   don't collide), and widen the drift-guard allowlist to the plugin-local prefixes.
3. Delete the `css-plugins` `outSubdir`/`label` path; regenerate docs; re-run `docs:api:locales:claude`
   for the moved pages; browser-verify the CSS section shows `Components · Utilities · Rules ·
   Declarations · Plugins`.

## Verification (of the proposal deliverable)

- The proposal is a document — "verification" is accuracy: every cssdoc symbol it names
  (`KIND_GROUPS`, `buildSidebar`, `renderIndex`, `CssDocEntry.group`, `EmitCssApiOptions`,
  `mergeCssSidebar`, `RenderConfig`, `cssDocSchema`) was confirmed present in `@cssdoc/*@0.7.8` under
  `node_modules/.pnpm/@cssdoc+*/dist/`.
- On approval: write the proposal to `docs/internal/proposals/cssdoc-custom-groups.md`; do not modify
  pantoken's docs pipeline yet (that's the post-ship follow-up).

Done — merged to main as PR [#11](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/11) (`4fa3e2b`).

## What landed

The plugin records now live **inside** the CSS API section as a Plugins subsection, using the cssdoc 0.7.9 `@group` feature — the exact design from our upstream proposal:

**CSS → Components · Utilities · Rules · Declarations · Plugins**

- **Tagged each plugin record `@group Plugins`** in the five `plugins/pantoken/*/scripts/generate.ts` blocks. 0.7.9 groups by `@group` (falling back to kind), so the five mixed-kind plugin records collapse into one group, ordered last.
- **Collapsed the two `emitCssApi` calls into one** in `build-css-api.ts` — plugin sheets join the single `"CSS"` section, `resolveSource`/`importSnippet` merged into name-keyed lookups, with an explicit `groups` order. Pages moved from `/api/css-plugins/*` to `/api/css/*`; the separate top-level section is gone.
- **hu translation** for the six changed blocks (each plugin page gained a `**Group:** Plugins` meta line); drift and parity green.

## Verified

- `vp check` clean; cssdoc lint accepts `@group`; the stale `css-plugins` tree is cleaned by TypeDoc.
- Browser-checked the live nav: the CSS section's children render as exactly `Overview · Components · Utilities · Rules · Declarations · Plugins`, and `/api/css/stacking` shows `Group: Plugins` with the right `@import`.
- CI green. **No release needed** — the plugin `scripts/` aren't in the published package (only `dist`), and the minified dist sheets strip doc comments, so the npm artifacts are unchanged; everything else is docs/build tooling.

One nice outcome: because 0.7.9 shipped the proposal's default ordering (kinds first, then custom `@group` groups), the layout you wanted fell out without even needing the explicit `groups` option — I passed it anyway to make the intent self-documenting.
